  • Type: DOUBLE
  • Default: 0.0
  • Options:
    • NONE
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

docs.title: FIELD_TAU
docs.text:
The value of \(\tau\) (in atomic units of time) for the Gaussian impulse field. INPUT SECTION: $tdks

  • Type: DOUBLE
  • Default: 800.0
  • Options:
    • NONE
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

docs.title: FIELD_FREQUENCY
docs.text:
The frequency \(\omega\) of the external field, in eV units. INPUT SECTION: $tdks

  • Type: DOUBLE
  • Default: 6.0
  • Options:
    • NONE
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

docs.title: FIELD_DIRECTION
docs.text:
The direction of the external applied field vector. INPUT SECTION: $tdks

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: NONE
  • Options:
    • XYZ: Pulse along the direction {1, 1, 1}
    • X: Pulse along the direction {1, 0, 0}
    • Y: Pulse along the direction {0, 1, 0}
    • Z: Pulse along the direction {0, 0, 1}

docs.title: FIELD_PARTICLE
docs.text:
The subsystem on which to apply the external field perturbation. INPUT SECTION: $tdks

  • Type: STRING

    • BOTH: Electrons and quantized protons
    • ELECTRONS
    • PROTONS
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

docs.title: 13.5.2.9 NEO-DFT(V)
docs.text:
By quantizing select nuclei, NEO gives rise to a potential energy surface with fewer nuclear degrees of freedom, which prevents a direct calculation of the vibrational frequencies of the entire molecule. Consequently, diagonalization of a coordinate Hessian in the NEO framework yields vibrational frequencies and accompanying normal modes of only the classical nuclei, with the quantum nuclei responding instantaneously to the motion of the classical nuclei.[1216] Although the fundamental anharmonic vibrational frequencies of the quantum nuclei can be accurately obtained through LR-NEO-TDDFT,[288] the couplings between the vibrations of the classical and quantum nuclei are missing. To obtain the fully coupled molecular vibrations, an effective strategy denoted NEO-DFT(V) was developed.[1520]

The NEO-DFT(V) method has been shown to incorporate key anharmonic effects in full molecular vibrational analyses and to produce accurate molecular vibrational frequencies compared to experiments.[1520]

The NEO-DFT(V) method involves diagonalization of an extended NEO Hessian composed of partial second derivatives of the coordinates of the classical nuclei (\(\mathbf{r}_{c}\)) and the expectation values of the quantum nuclei (\(\mathbf{r}_{q}\)). This extended Hessian matrix is composed of three sub-matrices: \(\textbf{H}_{0}=(\partial^{2}E/\partial\mathbf{r}^{2}_{c})|_{\mathbf{r}_{c}=\mathbf{r}_{q}}\), \(\textbf{H}_{1}=\partial^{2}E/\partial\mathbf{r}_{q}\partial\mathbf{r}_{c}\), and \(\textbf{H}_{2}=\partial^{2}E/\partial\mathbf{r}^{2}_{q}\), where in each case, all other coordinates of the classical nuclei and expectation values of the quantum nuclei are fixed. The extended Hessian has the following structure:

\[ \mathbf{H}_{\text{DFT(V)}}=\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{H}_{\text{0}}&\mathbf{H}^{\top}_{\text{1}}\\ \mathbf{H}_{\text{1}}&\mathbf{H}_{\text{2}}\end{bmatrix} \tag{13.67} \]

where

\[ \displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{\text{2}} \tag{13.68a} \]

The quantity \(\mathbf{R}=d\mathbf{r}_{q}/d\mathbf{r}_{c}\) and the NEO Hessian matrix is \(\mathbf{H}_{\text{NEO}}=d^{2}E/d\mathbf{r}^{2}_{c}\) (without the constraint that the expectation values of the quantum nuclei are fixed). In the expression for the \(\mathbf{H}_{\text{2}}\) matrix, \(\mathbf{M}\) is the diagonal mass matrix, and \(\mathbf{\Omega}\) is the diagonal matrix with elements corresponding to the squares of the LR-NEO-TDDFT fundamental vibrational frequencies.[1520] \(\mathbf{U}\) is a unitary matrix that transforms \(\mathbf{\Omega}\) to the target coordinate system and is approximated with the transition dipole moment vectors afforded by a LR-NEO-TDDFT calculation.[289]

Diagonalization of \(\mathbf{H}_{\text{DFT(V)}}\) produces the fully coupled molecular vibrational frequencies including anharmonic effects associated with the quantum protons. NEO-SCF(V) calculations can be invoked by setting NEO_SCFV = TRUE:

docs.title: NEO_SCFV
docs.text:
Enable a NEO-SCFV calculation

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 0 No NEO-SCFV calculation.
  • Options:
    • 1 Enable a NEO-SCFV calculation.: 0 Disable a NEO-SCFV calculation.
  • Recommendation: None.

In addition, the variables for NEO-HF 13.5.2.1 (or NEO-DFT 13.5.2.2) should be included, and JOBTYPE should be set to FREQ. Furthermore, the NEO-HF(V) method involves building the extended NEO-Hessian based on the NEO-HF Hessian and inputs from NEO-TDHF, and therefore the variables specific to LR-NEO-TDHF (TDDFT) ( 13.5.2.7) can be also be used to tune the calculation.

docs.title: 13.5.2.10 NEO-CC
docs.text:
An alternative route for inclusion of correlation effects between quantum particles (i.e., electrons and protons) is with wave functions methods that are systematically improvable and parameter-free.[1437]

Among the various developed multicomponent wave function methods, the NEO coupled cluster (NEO-CC) methods have been particularly successful.[1050]

The NEO-CC wave function is given by

\[ |\Psi_{ ext{NEO-CC}} angle=e^{\hat{T}}|0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}} angle, ag{13.69} \]

where \(\hat{T}\) is the cluster operator that incorporates the correlation effects between quantum particles, and \(|0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}} angle\) is the NEO-HF reference wave function. In the NEO-CCSD method,[1050] the cluster operator is given by

\[ \hat{T}=\hat{T}_{1}+\hat{T}_{2}=t^{i}_{a}a_{i}^{a}+t^{I}_{A}a_{I}^{A}+ rac{1}{4}t^{ij}_{ab}a_{ij}^{ab}+ rac{1}{4}t^{IJ}_{AB}a_{IJ}^{AB}+t^{iI}_{aA}a_{iI}^{aA}=\sum_{\alpha}t_{\alpha}a^{\alpha}, ag{13.70} \]

where \(a^{\alpha}=a^{\dagger}_{\alpha}=\{a_{i}^{a},a_{I}^{A},a_{ij}^{ab},a_{IJ}^{AB},a_{iI}^{aA}\}\) are the excitation operators expressed in terms of creation/annihilation (\(a^{\dagger}_{p}/a_{p}\)) fermionic operators, and \(\alpha\) is the excitation rank. Here, the \(i,j,\ldots\) indices denote occupied electronic orbitals, the \(a,b,\ldots\) indices denote unoccupied electronic orbitals, and the \(p,q,\ldots\) indices denote general electronic orbitals. The protonic orbitals are denoted analogously using the capitalized indices. The unknown \(t_{\alpha}\) wave function parameters (amplitudes) are determined by solving the set of nonlinear equations for each \(\alpha\):[1050]

\[ \langle 0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}}|a_{\alpha}e^{-\hat{T}_{1}-\hat{T}_{2}}\hat{H}_{ ext{NEO}}e^{\hat{T}_{1}+\hat{T}_{2}}|0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}} angle=0\;. ag{13.71} \]

In this equation, \(H_{ ext{NEO}}=h^{p}_{q}a_{p}^{q}+ rac{1}{2}g^{pq}_{rs}a_{pq}^{rs}+h^{P}_{Q}a_{p}^{q}+ rac{1}{2}g^{PQ}_{RS}a_{PQ}^{RS}-g^{pP}_{qQ}a_{pP}^{qQ}\) is the second-quantized NEO Hamiltonian, where \(h^{p}_{q}=\langle q|\hat{h}^{ ext{e}}|p angle\) and \(g^{pq}_{rs}=\langle rs|pq angle\) are conventional electronic core Hamiltonian and two-electron integrals, respectively. The remaining protonic (\(h^{P}_{Q}\) and \(g^{PQ}_{RS}\)) and electron-proton (\(g^{pP}_{qQ}\)) integrals are defined analogously. Lastly, the NEO-CCSD energy is calculated from

\[ E_{ ext{NEO-CCSD}}= ig{\langle}0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}} ig{|}e^{-\hat{T}_{1}-\hat{T}_{2}}\hat{H}_{ ext{NEO}}e^{\hat{T}_{1}+\hat{T}_{2}} ig{|}0^{ ext{e}}0^{ ext{p}} ig{ angle}\;. ag{13.72} \]

Accuracy can be improved by adding the triples terms to the NEO-CC cluster operator,[1053]

\[ \hat{T}_{3}=\hat{T}_{ ext{eep}}+\hat{T}_{ ext{epp}}+\hat{T}_{ ext{eee}}+\hat{T}_{ ext{ppp}}= rac{1}{4}t^{ijI}_{abA}a_{ijI}^{abA}+ rac{1}{4}t^{iIJ}_{aAB}a_{iIJ}^{aAB}+ rac{1}{36}t^{ijk}_{abc}a_{ijk}^{abc}+ rac{1}{36}t^{IJK}_{ABC}a_{IJK}^{ABC}. ag{13.73} \]

Each triples term can in principle be included explicitly, giving NEO-CCSDT, or as a perturbative correction, yeilding NEO-CCSD(T). Particularly important for capturing electron–proton correlation are the mixed \(\hat{T}_{ ext{eep}}\) and \(\hat{T}_{ ext{epp}}\) terms. The electonic triples term yeild quantitative corrections to the correlation energy, while protonic triples are considered to be negligible.

To increase the computational efficiency and reduce the memory requirements for the NEO-CCSD method, the two-particle integrals can be approximated with the density fitting (DF) approximation,[1055] in which the two-particle four-center integrals are factorized into a sum of products of three-center and two-center two-particle integrals. In particular, the four-center two-electron integrals are approximated by

\[ (\mu u| ho\sigma)=\langle\mu ho| u\sigma angle\approx\sum_{XY}(\mu u|X)(X|Y)^{-1}(Y| ho\sigma)\;, ag{13.74} \]

where \((\mu u|X)\) and \((X|Y)\) are three-center and two-center two-electron integrals, respectively. In this equation, \(\mu, u,\ldots\) and \(X,Y,\ldots\) indices denote electronic and auxiliary electronic basis functions, respectively. The four-center two-proton integrals are approximated analogously by

\[ (\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}| ho^{\prime}\sigma^{\prime})=\langle\mu^{\prime} ho^{\prime}| u^{\prime}\sigma^{\prime} angle\approx\sum_{X^{\prime}Y^{\prime}}(\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}|X^{\prime})(X^{\prime}|Y^{\prime})^{-1}(Y^{\prime}| ho^{\prime}\sigma^{\prime})\;, ag{13.75} \]

where primed indices denote protonic basis functions and \((\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}|X)\) and \((X^{\prime}|Y^{\prime})\) are three-center and two-center two-proton integrals, respectively. Finally, the four-center electron-proton integrals are approximated as

\[ (\mu u|\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime})=\langle\mu\mu^{\prime}| u u^{\prime} angle\approx\sum_{X^{\prime}Y^{\prime}}(\mu u|X^{\prime})(X^{\prime}|Y^{\prime})^{-1}(Y^{\prime}|\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}). ag{13.76} \]

By employing the DF approximation, the memory requirements for storing four-center two-particle integrals are reduced from \(N_{ ext{bf}}^{4}\) to \(N_{ ext{bf}}^{2} imes N_{ ext{aux}}\), where \(N_{ ext{bf}}\) and \(N_{ ext{aux}}\) are the number of electronic or protonic basis functions and auxiliary basis functions, respectively.[1055]

NEO-RICCSD is activated by NEO_RICCSD=1 or NEO-RICCSDT\({}_{\mathrm{eep,epp}}\) is activated by NEO_RICCSDTeepepp=1, to also include full electron–electron–proton and electron–proton–proton triple excitations. When one of these options is set, NEO_RICC_PT=1 can be set as well to enable a perturbative triples correction, corresponding to the NEO-RICCSD(T) method or the NEO-RICCSDT\({}_{\mathrm{eep,epp}}\)(T\({}_{\mathrm{eee}}\)) method, respectively. Note that triple protonic excitations are not calculated in any case, as they are expected to be negligible. The options for NEO-HF must be set also, (NEO=TRUE and METHOD=HF).

Geometry optimizations can be performed with gradients calculated by finite difference of energies, this requires JOBTYPE=OPT AND IDERIV=0.

docs.text:
Enable a NEO-RICCSD calculation.

Enable a NEO-RICCSDT \({}_{\mathrm{eep,epp}}\) calculation.

docs.title: NEO_RICC_PT
docs.text:
Enable a perturbative triples correction for a NEO-RICC calculation.

The following additional $rem variables can also be used to customize the NEO-RICC calculation (also see the examples in Section 13.5.6):

docs.title: NEO_CCSD_MAX_CYCLES
docs.text:
Controls the maximum number of CC iterations permitted.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 5000
  • Options:
    • \(n\): Set the maximum number of iterations to \(n>0\) .
  • Recommendation: None

docs.title: NEO_CCSD_CONVERGENCE
docs.text:
NEO-RICCSD is considered converged when the energy error is less than \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_CCSD\_CONVERGENCE}}\) .

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 8
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: None

docs.title: N_FROZEN_CORE
docs.text:
Sets the number of frozen core electronic orbitals in a NEO-RICC calculation.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: FC
  • Options:
    • FC: Frozen Core approximation (all core orbitals frozen).
    • \(n\): Freeze
    • \(n\): core orbitals (if set to 0, all electrons will be active).
  • Recommendation: Use default. This option only applies when NEO_RICCSD=1 or/and NEO_RICCSDTeepepp=1.

docs.title: 13.5.2.11 NEO-MP2
docs.text:
Second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory provides a useful framework for wave function based correlation effects with lower cost than NEO-CC [1332] . The NEO-MP2 correlation energy is composed of the electron-electron, proton-proton and electron-proton contributions:

\[ E_{\mathrm{NEO}}^{(2)}=E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{(2)}+E_{\mathrm{pp}}^{(2)}+E_{\mathrm{ep}}^{(2)}, \tag{13.77} \]

where

\[ \displaystyle E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{(2)} \tag{13.78a} \]

Here, \(i\) and \(j\) are occupied electronic spin orbitals with energies \(\varepsilon_{i}\) and \(\varepsilon_{j}\), \(a\) and \(b\) are virtual (unoccupied) electronic spin orbitals with energies \(\varepsilon_{a}\) and \(\varepsilon_{b}\), and uppercase indices indicate the analogous protonic spin orbitals and energies.

To provide accuracy that is competitive with NEO-CCSD, NEO-MP2 has been extended to include orbital optimization and empirical spin-component and electron-proton correlation scaling.[1054] This leads to the NEO equivalents of SOS-OOMP2 (O2)[852] and SOS-MP2[491] (Sections 6.6.5 and 6.6.6). The NEO equivalents are referred to as NEO-SOS\({}^{\prime}\)-OOMP2 and NEO-SOS\({}^{\prime}\)-MP2 to indicate the inclusion of an electron-proton correlation scaling factor:

\[ E_{\mathrm{NEO}}^{(2)}=c_{\mathrm{ss}}E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{\mathrm{ss}(2)}+c_{\mathrm{os}}E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{\mathrm{os}(2)}+c_{\mathrm{ep}}E_{\mathrm{ep}}^{(2)}+E_{\mathrm{pp}}^{(2)}, \tag{13.79} \]

where \(E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{\mathrm{ss}(2)}\) and \(E_{\mathrm{ee}}^{\mathrm{os}(2)}\) are the same- and opposite-spin parts of the electron-electron correlation energy, which are scaled by \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{os}}\), respectively, and \(c_{\mathrm{ep}}\) is the electron-proton scaling factor.

Orbital optimization is performed by minimizing the NEO-MP2 energy with respect to the unitary operator \(e^{\hat{X}-\hat{X}^{\dagger}}\) formed from the rotation operator \(\hat{X}=\hat{X}^{\text{e}}+\hat{X}^{\text{p}}=x^{i}_{a}a^{a}_{i}+x^{I}_{A}a^{A}_{I}\), with \(\mathbf{x}=\{x^{i}_{a},x^{I}_{A}\}\) being the set of unknown electronic and protonic orbital rotation parameters. Optimal orbital rotation parameters are solved for by finding the stationary points of electronic and protonic orbital gradients \(\mathbf{w}_{\text{e}}\) and \(\mathbf{w}_{\text{p}}\), which have elements

\[ \displaystyle(\mathbf{w}_{\text{e}})^{i}_{a}=\frac{\partial E_{\text{NEO-MP2}}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial x^{a}_{i}}\Bigr{|}_{\mathbf{x}_{\text{e}}=0} \tag{13.80a} \]

and are solved in an alternating fashion until self-consistency is achieved. For computational efficiency, all NEO-MP2 methods are implemented with the density fitting approximation for two-particle integrals,[386] as described in more detail in Section 13.5.2.10.

Currently only JOBTYPE = SP is supported. NEO-MP2 methods are invoked with NEO_RIMP2 = 1 to run without orbital optimization and NEO_RIMP2 = 2 to run with orbital optimization. Additionally, the variables for NEO-HF (NEO = TRUE and METHOD = HF) should be included:

docs.title: NEO_RIMP2
docs.text:
Enable a NEO-MP2 or NEO-OOMP2 calculation.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 0
  • Options:
    • 2: Perform a NEO-OOMP2 calclulation.
    • 1: Perform a NEO-MP2 calculation.
    • 0: Disable this option.
  • Recommendation: Both electronic and protonic auxiliary basis sets must be specified.

Spin-component scaling settings are controlled with the SCS variable. Custom \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{os}}\) can be set with SSS_FACTOR and SOS_FACTOR, respectively, when SCS = 3 is set (arbitrary scaling). By default, \(c_{\mathrm{ep}}\) is set to the same value as \(c_{\mathrm{os}}\), but a custom electron-proton scaling factor can be input with the EP_FACTOR variable, which will always override the default set by SCS. These settings are as follows (also see the examples in Section 13.5.6):

docs.title: SCS
docs.text:
Set the type of spin-component scaling.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 0
  • Options:
    • 1: Turns on spin-component scaling with SCS ( \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}=0.33\) , \(c_{\mathrm{os}}=1.2\) ).
    • 2: Turns on spin-component scaling with SOS ( \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}=0.0\) , \(c_{\mathrm{os}}=1.2\) for MP2, \(c_{\mathrm{os}}=1.3\) for OOMP2).
    • 3: arbitrary SCS (set with SSS_FACTOR and SOS_FACTOR ).
    • 0: no spin-component scaling.
  • Recommendation: NONE

docs.title: SSS_FACTOR
docs.text:
Controls the strength of the same-spin component of the MP2 electron-electron correlation energy.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 1000000
  • Options:
    • \(n\): Corresponding to \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}=n/10^{6}\) .
  • Recommendation: NONE

docs.title: SOS_FACTOR
docs.text:
Controls the strength of the opposite-spin component of the MP2 electron-electron correlation energy.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 1000000
  • Options:
    • \(n\): Corresponding to \(c_{\mathrm{os}}=n/10^{6}\) .
  • Recommendation: NONE

docs.title: EP_FACTOR
docs.text:
Controls the strength of the electron-proton component of the NEO-MP2 correlation energy.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 1000000
  • Options:
    • \(n\): Corresponding to \(c_{\mathrm{ep}}=n/10^{6}\) .
  • Recommendation: NONE

The NEO-CC2 approach evaluates correlation energy with second-order perturbation theory within an iterative NEO-CC calculation.[1053]

Rather than variationally optimizing orbital coefficients as in NEO-OOMP2, NEO-CC2 captures orbital relaxation with the \(\hat{T}_{1}\) amplitude equations from NEO-CCSD, while evaluating \(\hat{T}_{2}\) amplitudes with a second-order truncation,

\[ \langle 0^{\text{e}}0^{\text{p}}|a_{2}e^{-\hat{T}_{1}}\hat{H}_{\text{NEO}}e^{\hat{T}_{1}}+[\hat{F},\hat{T}_{2}]|0^{\text{e}}0^{\text{p}}\rangle=0, \tag{13.81} \]

where \(\hat{F}\) is the NEO Fock operator, \(F^{p}_{q}a^{q}_{p}+F^{P}_{Q}a^{Q}_{P}\). NEO-CC2 provides ground-state properties with similar accuracy to NEO-OOMP2, and can similarly be improved with the same SOS\({}^{\prime}\) scaling, giving NEO-SOS\({}^{\prime}\)-CC2. The NEO-SOS\({}^{\prime}\)-CC2 framework has also been extended to provide protonic and electronic excited states within coupled cluster response theory.[385] This method currently can only be used on systems with a single quantum proton, and is not implemented with density fitting. The NEO-CC2 and its SOS\({}^{\prime}\) variant are controlled with the NEO_CC2 $rem variable:

    • 1: Enable this option.

By default, NEO_CC2 performs a ground-state calculation, but excited states can be enabled by specify how many to compute with SET_ROOTS. In addition to the existing *\(rem* variables controlling SOS\){}^{\prime}$ scaling, EP_EX_FACTOR is a separate scaling factor for exited-state electron–proton correlation within NEO-SOS\({}^{\prime}\)-CC2:

docs.title: 13.5.2.12 NEO Configuration Interaction
docs.text:
The NEO Configuration Interaction (NEO-CI) wave function is a linear combination of NEO configurations:

\[ \Psi^{\text{NEO}}(\mathbf{R}^{\text{c}})=\sum_{iI}c_{iI}\lvert\Phi_{i}^{\text{e}}\rangle\lvert\Phi_{I}^{\text{n}}\rangle \tag{13.82} \]

where \(\lvert\Phi_{i}^{\text{e}}\rangle\) is electronic determinant \(i\) and \(\lvert\Phi_{I}^{\text{n}}\rangle\) is nuclear determinant \(I\). The electronic determinant is composed of electronic orbitals and the nuclear determinant is composed of protonic orbitals.[873]

The NEO-CI wave function is almost always truncated to include only single, or single and double excitations into the virtual orbital space. In the single-reference case, the electronic and nuclear determinants use the NEO-HF electronic and nuclear orbitals, respectively. In the multi-reference case, the electronic and nuclear orbitals are optimized via NEO-MCSCF. The orbitals can be optimized for multiple states with state-averaging.

Available models include:

  • NEO-MCSCF(CASSCF,RASSCF)
  • NEO-CI
  • NEO-MR-CI
  • NEO-OOMRCI

In addition to setting NEO = TRUE, METHOD = HF, and JOBTYPE = SP, the job settings for these available models are controlled by the following $rem variables:

Level of Theory Implicit Electrostatic Empirical Pseudopotentials (Algorithm) Solvation Embedding Dispersion Correction NEO-HF/DFT ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ NEO-MSDFT – – – – CNEO ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ NEO Hartree Product ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ LR-NEO-TDHF/TDDFT – – – – RT-NEO-TDHF/TDDFT – ✓ ✓ ✓ NEO-SCF(V) – – – – NEO-CC – – – – NEO-MP2 – – – – NEO-CI – – – –

docs.title: 13.5.3.1 Implicit Solvation
docs.text:
Bulk solvent effects can be directly incorporated into NEO calculations through the application of various implicit solvation models (Section 11.2) within the NEO framework.[1470]

The polarizable continuum model (PCM) constitutes one family of implicit solvation models and itself encompasses several different formulations:[756]

C-PCM,[1375] IEF-PCM,[245]

SS(V)PE,[245] etc.[569]

In the PCM approach, the solute molecule is placed in a cavity that is embedded in dielectric continuum solvent, and the cavity surface is discretized into \(i\) tesserae grid points. The solvent response is represented by a partial charge \(q_{i}\) centered at each tesserae grid point \(\mathbf{s}_{i}\).[1363]

For each SCF iteration, the current electronic and protonic densities, together with the fixed classical nuclei, define the solute’s charge distribution. This charge distribution gives rise to the solute’s electrostatic potential \(V_{i}\) at each tesserae grid point:

\[ V_{i}=\sum_{A} rac{Z_{A}}{\left|\mathbf{R}_{A}-\mathbf{s}_{i} ight|}-\sum_{\mu u}P_{\mu u}^{ ext{e}}\int d\mathbf{r}_{ ext{e}} rac{\phi_{\mu}^{ ext{e}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{ ext{e}} ight)\phi_{ u}^{ ext{e}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{ ext{e}} ight)}{\left|\mathbf{r}_{ ext{e}}-\mathbf{s}_{i} ight|}+\sum_{\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}}P_{\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}}^{ ext{p}}\int d\mathbf{r}_{ ext{p}} rac{\phi_{\mu^{\prime}}^{ ext{p}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{ ext{p}} ight)\phi_{ u^{\prime}}^{ ext{p}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{ ext{p}} ight)}{\left|\mathbf{r}_{ ext{p}}-\mathbf{s}_{i} ight|}\;. ag{13.83} \]

The solute electrostatic potential is then used to compute \(q_{i}\) using standard PCM methods. Once obtained, the set of tesserae charges is included as an additional one-electron (one-proton) contribution to the electronic (protonic) Fock or analogous Kohn-Sham matrix:

\[ \displaystyle F^{ ext{e}, ext{solv}}_{\mu u} ag{13.84a} \]

where \(F^{ ext{e}, ext{0}}_{\mu u}\) and \(F^{ ext{p}, ext{0}}_{\mu^{\prime} u^{\prime}}\) refer to the gas-phase, electronic [Eq. (13.37a)] and protonic [Eq. (13.37b)] Fock or analogous Kohn-Sham matrix elements, respectively.

NEO-PCM calculations involve iterative, self-consistent convergence of the nuclear-electronic wave function in the presence of the dielectric continuum solvent. NEO-PCM analytic gradients and analytic Hessians are also implemented. The calculation can be invoked by setting SOLVENT_METHOD = PCM in the $rem input section. Non-electrostatic contributions to the solvation free energy can also be included by setting SOLVENT_METHOD = SMD:

docs.title: SOLVENT_METHOD
docs.text:
Sets the preferred solvent method.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: 0
  • Options:
    • 0: Do not use a solvation model.
    • PCM: Use an apparent surface charge, polarizable continuum model (Section 11.2.3 ).
    • SMD: Use SMD (Section 11.2.9.3 ).
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

The SMD approach builds upon PCM by including non-electrostatic interactions, namely the cavitation, dispersion, and solvent structure energy terms. A caveat is that SMD was originally parameterized to reproduce experimental free energies of solvation for conventional, electronic DFT calculations (i.e., solute nuclei represented as point charges).[281]

In the simplest approach, the cavity surface is discretized into point charges. However, a more sophisticated approach utilizing Gaussian-smeared charges is also supported.[753]

Selection of these various PCM schemes and related variables can be set in the following input sections. For NEO-PCM calculations, use the \(pcm* and *\)solvent input sections. For NEO-SMD calculations, use the \(pcm* and *\)smx input sections. The capabilities from Q-Chem’s solvation library have been inherited to work with NEO methods, and the full list of variables that have been tested to work with NEO are listed in the pages that follow. See Section 11.2 for more comprehensive information on these solvation models as well as consult John Herbert’s review article[569] to guide your selection. Lastly, examples on setting up a solvated NEO calculation can be found in Section 13.5.6.

The format of the \(pcm* section is analogous to the *\)rem section:

$pcm
  <Keyword>  <parameter/option>
$end

Note

The following job control variables belong only in the \(pcm*  section. Do not place them in the *\)rem section.

docs.title: Theory
docs.text:
Specifies the which polarizable continuum model will be used. INPUT SECTION: $pcm

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: CPCM
  • Options:
    • CPCM (or CPCM1): Conductor-like PCM of Ref.
    • 275: Cossi M. et al. J. Comput. Chem. (2003) ,
    • 24: , pp. 669 . Link , with \(f_{\varepsilon}=(\varepsilon-1)/\varepsilon\) .
    • CPCM2: Original conductor-like screening model of Ref. , with \(f_{\varepsilon}=(\varepsilon-1)/(\varepsilon+1/2)\) .
    • IEFPCM: IEF-PCM with an asymmetric \(\mathbf{K}\) matrix.
    • SSVPE: SS(V)PE model, equivalent to IEF-PCM with a symmetric \(\mathbf{K}\) matrix.
  • Recommendation: We recommend C-PCM with NEO methods. The IEF-PCM model is more exact and better suited for low-dielectric solvents, but analytic Hessians are not supported.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Specifies which surface discretization method will be used. INPUT SECTION: $pcm

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: SwiG
  • Options:
    • SwiG: Switching/Gaussian method
    • Spherical: Use a single, fixed sphere for the cavity surface.
    • Fixed: Use discretization point charges instead of smooth Gaussians.
  • Recommendation: Use the default.

docs.title: Solver
docs.text:
Specifies the algorithm used to solve the PCM equations. INPUT SECTION: $pcm

  • Options:
    • INVERSION: Direct matrix inversion
    • CG: Iterative conjugate gradient
  • Recommendation: Use the default.

  • Recommendation: Use the default.

  • Options:
    • Bondi: Use the (extended) set of Bondi radii (Ref.
    • 1186: Rowland R. S., Taylor R. J. Phys. Chem. (1996) ,
    • 100: , pp. 7384 . Link ).
    • FF: Use Lennard-Jones radii from a molecular mechanics force field.
    • UFF: Use radii from the Universal Force Field (Ref.
    • 1146: Rappé A. K. et al. J. Am. Chem. Soc. (1992) ,
    • 114: , pp. 10024 . Link ).

docs.title: 13.5.3.2 Electrostatic Embedding
docs.text:
A set of external charges can be incorporated into a NEO calculation by specifying the \(external_charges* input section along with setting QM_MM = TRUE in the *\)rem input section. The format is shown below and consists of Cartesian coordinates and the value of the point charge, with one charge per line. The charge is in atomic units and the coordinates are in Ångstroms, unless bohrs are selected by setting the $rem keyword INPUT_BOHR to TRUE. The external charges are rotated with the molecule into the standard nuclear orientation and are specified in the following format:

$external_charges
   x-coord1  y-coord1  z-coord1  charge1
   x-coord2  y-coord2  z-coord2  charge2
   x-coord3  y-coord3  z-coord3  charge3
$end

Note that the electric field and analytic gradients are automatically saved to disk when the \(external_charges* keyword is present. This therefore enables NEO-QM/MM calculations to be performed using **Q-Chem** paired an external, molecular mechanics package. When using an external, molecular mechanics driver, the following *\)rem keyword should be set to FALSE to avoid issues with double counting:

docs.title: SKIP_CHARGE_SELF_INTERACT

    • FALSE: Computes the electrostatic interactions among external charges.
  • Recommendation: None

docs.title: 13.5.3.3 Empirical Dispersion Correction
docs.text:
All of the available DFT-D empirical dispersion methods for modeling non-covalent interactions introduced in Section 5.7.3 have been extended to NEO (including analytic gradients and analytic Hessians) and can be requested via the $rem variable DFT_D, which is discussed below.

Two caveats are worth pointing out: First, note that the functional form of the DFT-D empirical dispersion potential, \(E^{\text{D}}_{\text{disp}}(R_{AB})\), is a sum over all pairwise atomic contributions. For convenience, our implementation of the DFT-D correction uses the positions of the quantum proton(s) basis function center(s) for computing the interatomic distances \(R_{AB}\).[816] Second, the DFT-D dispersion potentials have been parameterized for classical nuclei represented as point charges.

docs.title: 13.5.3.4 Pseudopotentials
docs.text:
Q-Chem’s Effective Core Potential (ECP) package has been integrated with the NEO method to enable the description of relativistic and core electronic effects for systems in which some of the atoms may bear pseudopotentials. This is done by adding an additional one-electron potential contribution, which serves to model the effects of the core electrons, into the electronic Fock or analagous Kohn-Sham matrix (also see Section 8.10). In both the electronic and protonic Fock or analogous Kohn-Sham matrices, the one-electron term corresponding to the interaction of electrons or quantum protons with the classical nucleus with an ECP utilizes the effective nuclear charge shielded by the core electrons.[817]

The following $rem variable controls which ECP is used:

docs.title: ECP
docs.text:
Defines the effective core potential and associated basis set to be used

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: No ECP
  • Options:
    • General, Gen: User defined. ( $ecp keyword required)
    • Symbol: Use standard ECPs discussed above.
  • Recommendation: ECPs are recommended for first row transition metals and heavier elements. Also consult Section 8.10 for more details.

docs.title: 13.5.5 Molecular Properties and Wave Function Analysis Tools for NEO Models
13.5.5 Molecular Properties and Wave Function Analysis Tools for NEO Models
docs.text:
(July 4, 2026)

Some of Q-Chem’s molecular properties and wave function analysis tools have been extended to NEO methods, which are invoked automatically and reported in the output file:

  • Mulliken population analysis for ground state
  • Molecular dipole moments and proton position expectation value for ground state
  • MolDen files for protonic density plot generation from ground state NEO-SCF calculations
  • MolDen files for protonic transition densities plot generation from excited-state LR-NEO-TDHF (TDDFT) calculations
  • Vibrational analysis (including isotopic substitution) using CNEO or NEO-SCF(V) Hessians

Protonic density MolDen files are not automatically generated, but can be enabled by specifying the following two \(rem* variables: MAKE_CUBE_FILES = TRUE and PLOTS = TRUE. Specifying these keywords will also generate **MolDen** files for electronic density visualization. The grid parameters used for generating the electronic density can be tuned through the *\)plots input section (refer to Section 10.5.4.1 for details). Note that at this time, the grid for protonic density generation cannot be customized by the user and is instead chosen automatically based on several predefined choices.

docs.title: 13.6.1 Overview
docs.text:
(July 4, 2026)

Effective Hamiltonians provide a powerful framework for coarse-grained representation of complex electronic structure and for making direct comparisons with the experimentally derived parameters. It is commonly used in magnetic systems.[877]

Following general theory of effective Hamiltonians,[877]

Ref. [1106] describes how effective Hamiltonians can be extracted from the EOM-CC wave functions by using Bloch’s formalism. This approach provides an exact map of the many-body electronic structure onto a selected model space, yielding rigorous effective Hamiltonians in this model space. Currently, only EOM-SF-CCSD wave functions and Heisenberg’s and Hubbard’s model spaces are supported. The implemented procedure is \(N\)-to-\(N\) map, meaning that the number of model states is the same as the number of electronic states used to build the effective Hamiltonian. In the case of the Heisenberg’s Hamiltonian, the number of states \(N\) should be the same as the number of open-shell electrons, since this is the number of open-shell configurations that a single spin-flipping excitation can provide. In the case of the Hubbard’s Hamiltonian, \(N\) should equal to the total number of configurations that a single spin-flipping excitation can generate in the open-shell subspace (squared number of open-shell orbitals). Once CC_MAKE_EFF_HAM \(rem* variable is set to 1, the electronic states are read from the list specified in the *\)eff_ham section. Right and left amplitudes of these EOM states are used for the effective Hamiltonian construction. The Hamiltonians are constructed in two forms: the Bloch’s form (non-Hermitian) and des Cloizeaux’s form (Hermitian). If CC_OSFNO is invoked (recommended), the correspondence between the open-shell orbitals is established through the SVD procedure,[1104] followed by Boys’ localization of these orbitals. If these orbitals are desired, the orbital canonicalization should be disabled with CC_CANONIZE = FALSE. If GUI is set to 2, the orbitals used in CCMAN2 calculations are dropped to the .fchk file and can be visualized by IQmol.

Note

Beware that localization procedure may fail when there are several orbitals residing on the same radical centers, since in this case Boys localization becomes ill-conditioned.

The syntax of the \(eff_ham* section is similar to the syntax of the *\)trans_prop section. First, state_list starts the list of electronic states that are used for the construction of the effective Hamiltonian. The EOM states are abbreviated by the type of the method (currently, only SF_STATES is supported), its irreducible representation (use 1 for OSFNO and localized orbitals), and the number in the particular irreducible representation. The list of states is terminated by end_list. The type of the effective Hamiltonian is specified by the eff_ham keyword, which can be either Heisenberg or Hubbard.

The example below is based on Molecule 1 from Ref. [1106] . It shows how the Heisenberg Hamiltonian can be constructed from the EOM-SF-CCSD wave-functions. It can be modified to construct the Hubbard Hamiltonian by (\(i\)) requesting four SF states (that would include two covalent and two ionic states) and (\(ii\)) setting eff_ham to Hubbard.

docs.title: 13.5.4 Job Control for the NEO methods
13.5.4 Job Control for the NEO methods
13.5.4.1 General Keywords
docs.text:
The NEO method is a natural extension of the SCF method and it inherits many of its functionalities. Some keywords that are used in the SCF Job Control are used in the NEO methods with a few additional keywords. The following $rem variables must be specified in order to run NEO calculations:

Note

Some $rem variables, which we find mostly self-explanatory but not discussed below, that also influence NEO jobs in regards to geometry and symmetry considerations include INPUT_BOHR, SYM_IGNORE, and POINT_GROUP_SYMMETRY.

docs.title: NEO
docs.text:
Enable a NEO-SCF calculation.

  • Type: BOOLEAN
  • Default: FALSE
  • Options:
    • TRUE: Enable a NEO-SCF calculation.
    • FALSE: Disable a NEO-SCF calculation.
  • Recommendation: Set to TRUE if desired.

docs.title: JOBTYPE
docs.text:
Specifies the type of calculation.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: SP
  • Options:
    • SP: Single point energy.
    • FORCE: Analytical force calculation.
    • OPT: Geometry minimization.
    • TS: Transition structure search.
    • FREQ: Frequency calculation.
  • Recommendation: Application-dependent. Always use POINT_GROUP_SYMMETRY = FALSE with geometry optimization.

docs.title: METHOD
docs.text:
Specifies the exchange-correlation functional.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: No default
  • Options:
    • NAME: Use =
    • NAME: , where
    • NAME: is one of the following: HF for Hartree-Fock theory; one of the DFT methods listed in Section 5.3.5 .;
  • Recommendation: In general, consult the literature to guide your selection. Our recommendations for DFT are indicated in bold in Section 5.3.5 .

docs.title: BASIS
docs.text:
Specifies the electronic basis sets to be used.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: No default basis set
  • Options:
    • General, Gen: User defined ( $basis keyword required).
    • Symbol: Use standard basis sets as per Chapter
    • 8: .
    • Mixed: Use a mixture of basis sets (see Chapter
    • 8: ).
  • Recommendation: Consult literature and reviews to aid your selection.

The format for the user-defined basis section is as follows:

$basis \(X\) 0 \(L\) \(K\) \(scale\) \(\alpha_{1}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\alpha_{2}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\ddots\) \(\vdots\) \(\alpha_{K}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) **** $end

where

\(X\) Atomic symbol of the atom (atomic number not accepted) \(L\) Angular momentum symbol (S, P, SP, D, F, G) \(K\) Degree of contraction of the shell (integer) \(scale\) Scaling to be applied to exponents (default is 1.00) \(\alpha_{i}\) Gaussian primitive exponent (positive real number) \(C_{i}^{L}\) Contraction coefficient for each angular momentum (non-zero real numbers).

Atoms are terminated with **** and the complete basis set is terminated with the $end keyword terminator. No blank lines can be incorporated within the general basis set input. Note that more than one contraction coefficient per line is required for compound shells like SP. As with all Q-Chem input deck information, all input is case-insensitive.

Additionally, the NEO-SCF methods require definition of the nuclear basis sets. Refer to Ref. [1536] for selection of the protonic basis sets. Note that the pure (spherical harmonic) and Cartesian angular forms for the protonic basis sets are found in the main article and in the supported information, respectively. Also, see details about the NEO_PURECART variable described in the next section.

The format for the user-defined neo_basis section is as follows:

$neo_basis \(X\) 0 \(L\) \(K\) \(scale\) \(\alpha_{1}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\alpha_{2}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\ddots\) \(\vdots\) \(\alpha_{K}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) **** $end

Note

Several of the post-NEO-HF methods utilizing density fitting also require the nuclear auxiliary basis set to be defined. The format for such user-defined \(neo_aux_basis* section is identical to the *\)basis and $neo_basis input sections. See examples in Section 13.5.6 for more details.

docs.title: 13.5.4.2 Additional Keywords
docs.text: More $rem variables that can be used to customize the calculation. Some of these are NEO specific variables, while others are shared with other Q-Chem modules:

docs.title: BASIS_LIN_DEP_THRESH
docs.text:
Sets the threshold for determining linear dependence in the basis set

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 6
  • Options:
    • \(n\): Sets the threshold to \(10^{-n}\)
  • Recommendation: Set to 5 or smaller if you have a poorly behaved SCF and you suspect linear dependence in you basis set. Lower values (larger thresholds) may affect the accuracy of the calculation.

docs.title: NEO_BASIS_LIN_DEP_THRESH
docs.text:
This keyword is used to set the liner dependency threshold for nuclear basis sets. It is defined as \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_BASIS\_LIN\_DEP\_THRESH}}\) .

  • Type: DOUBLE
  • Default: 5.0
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: No recommendation.

docs.title: PURECART
docs.text:
INTEGER

  • Type: Controls the use of pure (spherical harmonic) or Cartesian angular forms
  • Default: 1111
  • Options:
    • \(hgfd\): Use 1 for pure and 2 for Cartesian.
  • Recommendation: This is pre-defined for all standard basis sets

docs.title: NEO_PURECART
docs.text:
This keyword is used to specify Cartesian or spherical Gaussians for nuclear basis functions.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 2222
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: The default value corresponds to the use of Cartesian Gaussians for all angular momentum classes. The value = 1111 would use spherical Gaussians instead, similar to the use of PURECART .

docs.title: NEO_ISOTOPE
docs.text:
Enable calculations of different types of isotopes. Only one type of isotope is allowed at present.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 1
  • Options:
    • 1: This NEO calculation uses protons.
    • 2: This NEO calculation uses deuterons.
    • 3: This NEO calculation uses tritons.
  • Recommendation: Refer to the NEO literature for the best performance on the isotope effects calculations.

docs.title: NEO_VPP
docs.text:
This keyword is used to control whether to remove \(J-K\) terms from the nuclear Fock matrix and the corresponding kernel terms for NEO excited state methods. The purpose for the removal of these terms in the case of one quantum proton is to save on computational cost. Note that the ground state NEO-HF or NEO-DFT energy is the same with or without removal of these nuclear \(J-K\) terms. The nuclear virtual orbitals will however be different, which may affect the results for perturbative methods ( i.e. , multicomponent excited-state methods and post-NEO-HF wave function methods).

  • Type: LOGICAL/INTEGER
  • Default: TRUE
  • Options:
    • TRUE（或 1）: Enable this option (include nuclear \(J-K\) terms).
    • FALSE（或 0）: Disable this option (remove nuclear \(J-K\) terms).
  • Recommendation: Set = 0 only in the case of one quantum hydrogen.

docs.title: XC_GRID
docs.text:
Specifies the type of grid to use for DFT calculations.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: Functional-dependent; see Table
  • Options:
    • 0: Use SG-0 for H, C, N, and O; SG-1 for all other atoms.
    • \(n\): Use SG-
    • \(n\): for all atoms, \(n=1,2\) , or 3 \(XY\) A string of two six-digit integers \(X\) and \(Y\) , where \(X\) is the number of radial points and \(Y\) is the number of angular points where possible numbers of Lebedev angular points, which must be an allowed value from Table 5.2 in Section 5.5 . \(-XY\) Similar format for Gauss-Legendre grids, with the six-digit integer \(X\) corresponding to the number of radial points and the six-digit integer \(Y\) providing the number of Gauss-Legendre angular points, \(Y=2N^{2}\) .
  • Recommendation: We strongly recommend using an unpruned, Euler-Maclaurin-Lebedev grid type for NEO-DFT calculations. Larger grids may be required for optimization and frequency calculations.

docs.title: UNRESTRICTED
docs.text:
Controls the use of restricted or unrestricted orbitals.

  • Type: LOGICAL
  • Default: FALSE
  • Options:
    • FALSE: Constrain the spatial part of the alpha and beta orbitals to be the same.
    • TRUE: Do not Constrain the spatial part of the alpha and beta orbitals.
  • Recommendation: The ROHF method is not available. Note that for unrestricted calculations on systems with an even number of electrons it is usually necessary to break \(\alpha\) / \(\beta\) symmetry in the initial guess, by using SCF_GUESS_MIX or providing $occupied information (see Section 4.4 on initial guesses).

docs.title: S2THRESH
docs.text:
Cutoff for neglect of overlap integrals, defined via a two-electron shell-pair threshold of \(10^{-\mathrm{S2THRESH}}\) ( \(\leq 14\) ).

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: Same as
  • Options:
    • \(n\): for a threshold of \(10^{-n}\) .
  • Recommendation: Increase the value of if the program finds negative eigenvalues for the overlap matrix.

docs.title: THRESH
docs.text:
Cutoff for neglect of two electron integrals. \(10^{-\mathrm{THRESH}}\) ( \(\leq 14\) ).

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 8
  • Options:
    • \(n\): for a threshold of \(10^{-n}\) .
  • Recommendation: The value should satisfy \(\geq\) 3 + SCF_CONVERGENCE , although = 4 + SCF_CONVERGENCE is the default (in most cases) since Q-Chem v. 6.0. See Ref. 479 Gray M., Bowling P. E., Herbert J. M. J. Phys. Chem. A (2024) , 128 , pp. 7739 . Link for recommended values of in the presence of diffuse basis functions, where tighter thresholds are often required and too-loose thresholds may lead to slower convergence or convergence failure.

docs.title: MEM_STATIC
docs.text:
Sets the memory for AO-integral evaluations and their transformations in Q-Chem 4.1 or older versions.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 192
  • Options:
    • \(n\): User-defined number of megabytes.
  • Recommendation: Use the default.

docs.title: MEM_TOTAL
docs.text:
Sets the total memory available to Q-Chem , in megabytes.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 2000
  • Options:
    • \(n\): User-defined number of megabytes.
  • Recommendation: Use the default, or set to the physical memory of your machine. The minimum requirement is \(3X^{2}\) .

docs.title: 13.5.4.3 NEO-SCF Specific Keywords
docs.text: The following \(rem* variables can be used to specify the tolerances for NEO-SCF convergence. Some of these *\)rem variables are inherited from conventional SCF calculations:

docs.title: SCF_CONVERGENCE
docs.text:
NEO-SCF is considered converged when the electronic wave function error is less that \(10^{-\mathrm{SCF\_CONVERGENCE}}\) . Adjust the value of THRESH at the same time. (Starting with Q-Chem 3.0, the DIIS error is measured by the maximum error rather than the RMS error as in earlier versions.)

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 5
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: None.

docs.title: NEO_N_SCF_CONVERGENCE
docs.text:
NEO-SCF is considered converged when the nuclear wave function error is less that \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_N\_SCF\_CONVERGENCE}}\) .

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 7
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: None.

docs.title: NEO_E_CONV
docs.text:
Energy convergence criteria in the NEO-SCF calculations so that the difference in energy between consecutive iterations is less than \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_E\_CONV}}\) .

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 8
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: Tighter criteria for geometry optimization are recommended. Note that for stepwise calculations, this convergence criteria checks the difference in energy between electronic and protonic microiterations blocks.

docs.title: MAX_SCF_CYCLES
docs.text:
Controls the maximum number of SCF iterations permitted.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 50
  • Options:
    • \(n\): \(n>0\) User-selected.
  • Recommendation: Increase for slowly converging systems such as those containing transition metals.

docs.title: NEO_E_MAX_SCF_CYCLES
docs.text:
Controls the maximum number of electronic SCF micoiterations permitted. This variable is only used for stepwise NEO-SCF optimizations.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 150
  • Options:
    • \(n\): \(n>0\) User-selected.
  • Recommendation: None.

docs.title: NEO_N_MAX_SCF_CYCLES
docs.text:
Controls the maximum number of nuclear SCF micoiterations permitted. This variable is only used for stepwise NEO-SCF optimizations.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 150
  • Options:
    • \(n\): \(n>0\) User-selected.
  • Recommendation: None.

The NEO-SCF iteration procedure has traditionally involved solving the electronic and quantum nuclear Roothaan/Kohn-Sham equations in alternating fashion until convergence to the variational solution is reached. This approach can become computationally expensive, especially when many SCF iterations are required to achieve self-consistency. To accelerate this procedure, those equations may instead be solved simultaneously at every step of the NEO-SCF iteration procedure. This is now the default scheme for solving the NEO-SCF equations. We support the simultaneous implementation of the Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace (DIIS) algorithm[837]

as well as the Geometric Direct Minimization (GDM)[1391] approach. The following $rem variables permit some customization of the NEO-SCF iterations:

docs.title: NEO_SIMULTANEOUS_SCF
docs.text:
Enables simultaneous optimization algorithm.

  • Type: LOGICAL
  • Default: TRUE
  • Options:
    • TRUE
    • FALSE
  • Recommendation: Use the default unless issues with convergence are observed, in which cause set to FALSE to utilize the traditional stepwise approach.

docs.title: SCF_ALGORITHM
docs.text:
Algorithm used for converging the SCF.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: DIIS
  • Options:
    • DIIS: Pulay DIIS.
    • GDM: Geometric Direct Minimization.
    • DIIS_GDM: Use DIIS and then later switch to geometric direct minimization.
  • Recommendation: In the NEO methods, the GDM procedure is recommended. Note that DIIS_GDM is only supported for simultaneous optimizations.

docs.title: NEO_SCF_GUESS_N
docs.text:
Specifies the initial guess procedure for the nuclear orbitals in a NEO-SCF calculation.

  • Type: STRING
  • Default: TIGHT
  • Options:
    • CORE: Diagonalize the nuclear core Hamiltonian
    • TIGHT: Occupies the least diffuse nuclear MO
    • AUTOSAD: On-the-fly superposition of nuclear atomic densities from an atomic NEO calculation
    • READ: Read previous nuclear MOs from disk
  • Recommendation: Use the default. Note that if is set to READ , only the nuclear MOs from a previous NEO-SCF job are read from disk. The starting guess for the electronic MOs in a NEO calculation remains the converged result from the conventional electronic calculation of the current job. To read in both the electronic and nuclear MOs from a previous NEO-SCF job, must be set to READ in conjunction with SKIP_SCFMAN set to TRUE .

docs.title: NEO_STEPWISE_SCF_STEPS
docs.text:
Specifies the number of NEO-SCF stepwise/alternating macro-iterations to perform before switching to simultaneous algorithm.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 0
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: The rate of convergence of the NEO-SCF procedure is dependent on the initial guess for the electronic and protonic orbitals. For especially difficult systems, it may be helpful to do stepwise optimization before switching to simultaneous.

Note

The following variables are specific to SCF_ALGORITHM = DIIS.

docs.title: DIIS_SUBSPACE_SIZE
docs.text:
Controls the size of the DIIS subspace during the SCF.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 10
  • Options:
    • User-defined
  • Recommendation: None.

docs.title: DIIS_ERR_RMS
docs.text:
Changes the DIIS convergence metric from the maximum to the RMS error.

  • Type: LOGICAL
  • Default: FALSE
  • Options:
    • TRUE
    • FALSE
  • Recommendation: Use the default, the maximum error provides a more reliable criterion.

Note

The following variables are specific to SCF_ALGORITHM = DIIS_GDM.

docs.title: MAX_DIIS_CYCLES
docs.text:
The maximum number of DIIS iterations before switching to (geometric) direct minimization.

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 50
  • Options:
    • 1: Only a single Roothaan step before switching to (G)DM
    • \(n\)
    • \(n\): DIIS iterations before switching to (G)DM.
  • Recommendation: None

docs.title: THRESH_DIIS_SWITCH
docs.text:
The threshold for switching between DIIS extrapolation and direct minimization of the SCF energy is \(10^{-\mbox{{\small THRESH\_DIIS\_SWITCH}}}\) .

  • Type: INTEGER
  • Default: 2
  • Options:
    • User-defined.
  • Recommendation: None

docs.title: A.1.1 概述
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

在 Q-Chem 程序中，开发了一个原子轨道积分（Atomic Orbital integrals，AOInts）软件包。该包对用户而言几乎不可见，却是 Q-Chem 程序整体速度与效率的关键之一。其核心挑战已被 Gill 精辟地总结:[445]

自 Boys 于 1950 年将高斯基组引入量子化学以来，高斯函数上那些臭名昭著的双电子排斥积分（ERIs）的计算与处理，一直是计算化学研究者进行科学研究的一条重要途径。事实上，实用计算机程序的出现，在很大程度上正是得益于那些精密算法的发展——正是这些算法使得计算中等甚至较小规模分子体系所需的数量极其庞大的 ERIs 成为可能。

任何一款具有竞争力的量子化学软件包，其 ERI 引擎都是整个软件包中最复杂的组成部分之一。鉴于此类引擎的效率至关重要，通过考察其 ERI 引擎的各个组件，就可以快速衡量出一个关于程序预期性能的有用参照标准。近年来，Q-Chem 公司的开发人员在推动 ERI 算法技术进步方面做出了重大贡献（例如，参见文献 [445]），因此 Q-Chem 的 AOInts 软件包被认为是同类中最先进的，这并不令人意外。

在 20 世纪 50 年代之前，将薛定谔波动力学系统地应用于化学时最困难的一步，就是计算那些衡量电子间排斥作用的臭名昭著的双电子积分。Boys[153] 表明，如果在基组中使用高斯型轨道（Gaussian orbitals）而非 Slater 型轨道（Slater orbitals），这一步骤可以变得更容易（尽管仍然耗时）。继那篇具有里程碑意义的计算化学论文[152]（同样出自 Boys）之后，人们构建出了能够计算用 \(s\) 和 \(p\) 轨道处理一般多原子分子时出现的所有 ERIs 的程序。然而，这些程序运行极其缓慢，只能应用于最小的分子体系。

1969 年，Pople 构建了一种突破性的 ERI 算法，其速度比先前的算法快一百倍。该算法在其相关积分类别中至今仍是最快的，现被称为 Pople-Hehre 轴切换（axis-switch）方法。[1114]

在 Pople 最初的开创性工作之后的二十年里，大量关于 ERI 构建的研究工作被记录下来，这些工作都建立在 Pople 原始成功的基础之上。本质上，新算法的进展可归结为两类：更好地处理角动量（\(L\)），或更好地处理收缩（contraction，\(K\)）；每一种新方法都提高了速度，并拓展了量子力学解决真实化学问题的应用范围。

到 1990 年，另一道屏障已经出现。当时的程序已变得十分精密，学术界和工业界都开始认识并使用 ab initio 量子化学的强大能力，但软件却深受"陈旧代码堆积综合征"（dusty deck syndrome）之苦，日益难以跟上硬件发展的快速进步。向量处理器、并行架构以及图形用户界面的出现，都对编程提出了截然不同的新要求，人们已经清楚地认识到，以一种全新的、从零开始的姿态是既不可避免又令人期待的。此外，积分瓶颈又以新的面目重新浮现，标准程序如今正撞上 \(N^{2}\) 这一堵墙。无论 ERIs 的计算速度有多快，一个无情的事实依然存在：所需的 ERIs 数目随体系规模呈平方（二次）标度增长。

Q-Chem 项目的建立正是为了解决这一问题，并寻找能够绕过 \(N^{2}\) 墙的新方法。人们寻求积分理论根本性的新方法，由此取得的持续进展[1463] 已使 Q-Chem 牢牢立足于该领域的前沿。不过需要强调的是，我们所发展的 \({\cal{O}}({N})\) 方法仍然需要短程 ERIs 来处理近邻电子之间的相互作用，因此现代 ERI 代码的重要性依然存在。

积分方法在时间上的发展与演变，可以通过一条列出重要新算法首次提出年份的时间线来概括。对这些算法最好的讨论方式是依据其能够高效计算的 ERI 或矩阵元的类型。

1950 Boys [153] 低 \(L\)、低 \(K\) 的 ERIs 1969 Pople [1114] 低 \(L\)、高 \(K\) 的 ERIs 1976 Dupuis [358] 任意 \(L\)、低 \(K\) 的积分 1978 McMurchie [934] 任意 \(L\)、低 \(K\) 的积分 1982 Almlöf [41] 引入直接 SCF（direct SCF）方法 1986 Obara [1004] 任意 \(L\)、低 \(K\) 的积分 1988 Head-Gordon [543] 任意 \(L\)、低 \(K\) 的积分 1991 Gill [445] 任意 \(L\)、任意 \(K\) 的积分 1994 White [1463] 以线性工作量计算 J 矩阵 1996 Schwegler [1222] 以线性工作量计算 HF 交换矩阵 1997 Challacombe [235] 以线性工作量计算 Fock 矩阵

docs.title: A.2.1 概述
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

针对高斯基函数分子积分这一领域，近期已有综述文献[452]， 若需更深入的讨论以及该一般领域的更多参考文献，请读者参阅该综述。本简短说明的目的是介绍基本方法， 特别是电子排斥积分（Electron Repulsion Integral, ERI）算法的实现，以及 Q-Chem 程序底层的 AOInts 软件包中用户所关心的各方面内容。

我们首先注意到，ab initio（从头算）计算中遇到的所有积分——其中最为人所知的有重叠积分、动能积分、 多极矩积分、核间排斥积分、核-电子吸引积分以及电子间排斥积分——均可写成如下一般形式

\[ (\mathbf{ab}|\mathbf{cd})=\int\phi_{\mathbf{a}}(\mathbf{r}_{1})\,\phi_{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{r}_{1})\,\theta(r_{12})\,\phi_{\mathbf{c}}(\mathbf{r}_{2})\,\phi_{\mathbf{d}}(\mathbf{r}_{2})\;d\mathbf{r}_{1}d\mathbf{r}_{2} \tag{A.1} \]

其中基函数为收缩高斯型函数（Contracted Gaussian Type Function, CGTF）

\[ \phi_{\mathbf{a}}(\mathbf{r})=(x-A_{x})^{a_{x}}(y-A_{y})^{a_{y}}(z-A_{z})^{a_{z}}\sum_{i=1}^{K_{a}}D_{ai}\,e^{-\alpha_{i}|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{A}|^{2}} \tag{A.2} \]

docs.title: A.2.2 数据结构：壳层对与壳层四元组
A.2.2 数据结构：壳层对（Shell Pairs）与壳层四元组（Quartets）
A.2.2.1 壳层对数据
docs.text:
通常通过收缩程度和角动量来表征左矢（bra）、右矢（ket）以及左矢-右矢（bra-ket）。一般而言，为壳层对（shell-pair）而非基函数对整理数据更为方便。壳层（shell）定义为具有相同指数和相同中心的基函数集合。例如，在许多基于 Pople 体系推导出的基组（Basis Set）中，四个基函数涵盖不同的角动量类型（即，\(s\)、\(p_{x}\)、\(p_{y}\)、\(p_{z}\)），它们位于同一原子中心并共享相同的指数，构成一个壳层。

壳层对数据集是现代积分程序取得成功的关键，主要原因有三。第一，在构建壳层对时，会考虑基组中的所有壳层对，并将其归类为显著（significant）或可忽略（negligible）。若所涉及的壳层彼此相距过远（相对于其弥散程度而言），其重叠可以忽略，则该壳层对被视为可忽略。考虑到高斯基函数的衰减速率，大分子中大多数壳层对都可忽略也就不足为奇了，也就是说，显著壳层对的数量随分子尺寸呈线性增长。第二，电子排斥积分（Electron Repulsion Integral, ERI）算法中频繁需要的若干有用中间量，应当在壳层对构建阶段一次性计算并作为壳层对信息的一部分存储，尤其是那些涉及代价高昂的除法运算的中间量。这避免了对简单量的重复求值。第三，按类型（即，角动量和收缩程度）对壳层对信息进行排序非常有用，其原因将在下文讨论。

Q-Chem 的壳层对构建提供了两种基本的积分壳层对截断判据选项：一种基于积分阈值（$rem 变量 THRESH），另一种相对于机器精度。

智能化构建壳层对数据的计算开销随基组规模呈线性增长，对于大型直接自洽场（Direct SCF）计算，其所需的相对 CPU 时间几乎完全可以忽略；而对于小型计算任务，该部分约占总任务时间的 10%。

docs.title: A.2.2.2 壳层四元组与积分类别
docs.text:
给定一个已排序的壳层对数据列表，可以通过将壳层对两两配对来构造所有可能重要的壳层四元组（shell-quartet）。由于壳层对已经排序，可以按批次处理同一类型或类别的积分（例如，\((ss|ss)\)、\((sp|sp)\)、\((dd|dd)\)、等等），其中积分类别由角动量（\(L\)）和收缩程度（\(K\)）共同表征。这种方法对于向量处理器以及半直接（semi-direct）积分算法非常有利：最昂贵（高 \(K\) 或高 \(L\)）的积分类别只需计算一次并存入内存（或磁盘），而在每次迭代中只需重建较廉价的类别。

尽管壳层对可能已经过仔细筛选，但两个显著壳层对所组成的壳层四元组仍有可能无需直接计算。共有三种情况：

  • 该四元组在点群对称性（point group symmetry）意义下与另一个已处理过的四元组等价。
  • 基于对最大四元组左矢-右矢廉价计算得到的 ERI 上界[449]， 该四元组可以被忽略。
  • 在增量式 Fock 矩阵构建的基础上，与该四元组关联的任一左矢-右矢所乘的最大密度矩阵元素可能小到可以忽略。

注意

显著性与可忽略性始终基于 $rem 变量 THRESH 所设定的积分阈值水平。

docs.title: A.2.3 电子排斥积分（ERI）计算综述
A.2.3 电子排斥积分（ERI）计算综述
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

以下各小节对 ERI 计算问题的各个方面进行了描述。

docs.title: A.2.3.1 基本 ERI
docs.text:
基本 ERI \([ss|ss]^{(0)}\equiv[\bm{0}]^{(0)}\) 是所有 ERI 算法的基础，通常表示为[452]

\[ [\bm{0}]^{(0)}=D_{A}D_{B}D_{C}D_{D}\int e^{-\alpha|\mathbf{r}_{1}-\mathbf{A}|^{2}}e^{-\beta|\mathbf{r}_{1}-\mathbf{B}|^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{r_{12}}\right)e^{-\gamma|\mathbf{r}_{2}-\mathbf{C}|^{2}}e^{-\delta|\mathbf{r}_{2}-\mathbf{D}|^{2}}\;d\mathbf{r}_{1}d\mathbf{r}_{2} \tag{A.3} \]

该积分可化为如下形式的一维积分

\[ [\bm{0}]^{(0)}=U(2\,{\vartheta}^{2})^{1/2}\left({\frac{2}{\pi}}\right)^{1/2}\,\int_{0}^{1}e^{-Tu^{2}}du \tag{A.4} \]

并可采用改进的切比雪夫（Chebyshev）插值方案高效计算[447]。 方程 (A.4) 还可推广到大多数计算所需的通用情形 \([\mathbf{0}]^{(m)}\) 积分。 在求得基本 ERI 之后，进而构建完整的括号（bra-ket）ERI（或中间矩阵元，见后文）时，需要解决角动量问题和收缩问题。

注意

方括号表示原（primitive）积分，圆括号表示完全收缩后的积分。

docs.title: A.2.3.2 角动量问题
docs.text: 基本积分本质上是不含角动量的积分（即，它是 \([ss|ss]\) 型积分）。角动量通常以 \(L\) 表示，一直是高效 ERI 构建中的难点，这一点在上文的时间线中已有体现。起初，角动量是通过对基本 ERI 关于核中心的某个笛卡尔坐标求导来计算的。这是一条极其低效的途径，但它确实可行，并且适用于 ERI 方法的早期发展阶段。递推关系[1004]和张量方程[22]是现代方法的基础。

docs.title: A.2.3.3 收缩问题
docs.text:
可以通过考察由 STO-3G 基组导出的 \(s\) 型函数的通用收缩 ERI 来描述收缩问题。每个基函数的收缩阶数为 \(K=3\)。于是该 ERI 可写为

\[ \displaystyle\begin{aligned} \displaystyle(ss|ss)&\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sum_{k=1}^{3}\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}D_{Ai}D_{Bj}D_{Ck}D_{D\ell}\\ &\displaystyle\qquad\times\int e^{-\alpha_{i}|\mathbf{r}_{1}-\mathbf{A}|^{2}}e^{-\beta_{j}|\mathbf{r}_{1}-\mathbf{B}|^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{r_{12}}\right)e^{-\gamma_{k}|\mathbf{r}_{2}-\mathbf{C}|^{2}}e^{-\delta_{\ell}|\mathbf{r}_{2}-\mathbf{D}|^{2}}d\mathbf{r}_{1}d\mathbf{r}_{2}\\ &\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sum_{k=1}^{3}\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}[s_{i}s_{j}|s_{k}s_{\ell}]\end{aligned} \tag{A.5} \]

单个 ERI 就需要 81 个原积分。对于收缩程度更高的基组（STO-6G、6-311G），该问题急剧加剧，这也正是壳层对（shell-pair）建模技术发展的动因，

即构造一个原函数数目少于第一个壳层的第二个壳层对，但相对于所要求的积分阈值不引入额外误差。

Pople-Hehre 坐标轴切换法[1114]对于高收缩、低角动量的积分类别非常优秀。

docs.title: A.2.4 电子排斥积分评估的效率
A.2.4 电子排斥积分（ERI）评估的效率
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

人们常说自洽场（SCF）计算的成本随体系规模以 \({\cal{O}}({N^{4}})\) 的速度增长，但这一说法是否成立，关键在于 \(N\) 的含义。在分子大小固定的情况下，由于电子排斥积分（ERI）数目 \((\mu\nu|\lambda\sigma)\) 的增长，计算成本可能呈现四次方 scaling。然而，在讨论电子结构计算的渐近成本时，人们更常指的是在基组（Basis Set）选择固定的前提下，成本随分子大小的变化关系。此时体系规模（\(N\)）以原子数来衡量，其渐近成本应为 \({\cal{O}}({N^{2}})\)，详见下文讨论。

docs.title: A.2.4.1 二次方标度
docs.text:
现代量子化学之所以能够取得定量化研究的巨大成功，超越其早期粗糙的定性阶段，可归功于两大源泉：更好的算法和更好的计算机。尽管这两项技术都在快速进步，但电子排斥积分（ERI）总数随分子体系大小呈二次方增长这一事实，严重阻碍了相关研究的努力。即便 ERI 算法效率大幅提升，也只能带来适用范围 moderate 的扩展，从而妨碍了 ab initio 方法更广泛地应用于或许具有生物化学意义的领域——在这些领域，半经验技术[323] 早已被证明极具价值。

因此，消除二次方标度算法成为整个 1990 年代量子化学众多研究工作的主题，并由此发展出许多旨在缓解该问题的替代算法。Johnson 率先实现了计算成本随体系大小线性增长的密度泛函理论（Density Functional Theory, DFT）交换/关联泛函。

这为该领域最重大的突破铺平了道路——线性标度的 CFMM 算法[1463] 带来了线性标度的 DFT 计算[1465] 。借助传统理论形式下的 QCTC[234] 与 ONX[1222] 算法，人们取得了进一步的突破，而更为激进的方法[23] 则可能为 ab initio 计算带来全新的途径。对二次方库仑问题的研究不仅产生了线性标度算法，还为理解许多分子能量组分的重要性提供了深刻见解。

线性标度的库仑以及 SCF 交换/关联算法并非故事的终点，因为 \({\cal{O}}({N^{3}})\) 的对角化步骤一直是半经验技术中的耗时瓶颈，并且有预测指出，在中期内它也将成为 ab initio 方法的耗时瓶颈[1317]。

不过，分而治之（divide-and-conquer）技术[1516]

以及近期开发的二次收敛 SCF 算法[1008]

为解决这一问题展现出很大的前景。

docs.title: A.2.4.2 算法选择
docs.text:
并不存在单一的 ERI 算法能够高效处理所有积分类别；相反，每种算法往往在某些特定的积分类别上表现优于其他备选方案。PRISM 算法[451]

是一整套错综复杂的路径与步骤的集合，其中所选路径是针对给定类别最高效的路径。看起来，某一给定积分类别的最适宜路径取决于收缩（contraction）步骤的相对位置（低收缩的 bra-ket 倾向于晚收缩，高收缩的 bra-ket 采用早收缩步骤效率最高）。

细致研究所给出的 FLOP 计数是当前积分算法选择的基础，但必须注意确保算法不受 MOPs 的限制[410]。 未来的算法选择准则将更多地考虑硬件的内存、磁盘、芯片架构、缓存大小、向量化与并行化特性，其中许多特性已存在于 Q-Chem 之中。

docs.title: A.2.4.3 更高效的 Hartree–Fock 梯度与 Hessian 评估
docs.text:
Q-Chem 结合了 Head-Gordon–Pople（HGP）方法[543] 与 COLD prism 方法[22] 来评估 Hartree-Fock 的梯度和 Hessian。所有双电子四中心积分按其角动量类型和收缩程度进行分类。对每一类积分，程序选择成本较低的方法。在实践中，梯度或 Hessian 计算中的大多数积分类别都选用 HGP 方法，因此它主导了总的 CPU 时间。

近期，Q-Chem 中的 HGP 代码被完全重写，用于评估梯度计算中的 P II\({}^{x}\) P 项以及 Hessian 计算中的 P II\({}^{xy}\) P 项。我们的重点是通过减少缓存未命中（cache miss）而非减少 FLOP 计数来提高代码效率。以下是 AZT（叠氮胸苷）分子上一个 Hartree-Fock 计算的一些计时结果。

基组 AIX Linux 梯度评估：P II${}^{x}$ P 项 旧版 新版 新版/旧版 旧版 新版 新版/旧版 3-21G 34 s 20 s 0.58 25 s 14 s 0.56 6-31G** 259 s 147 s 0.57 212 s 120 s 0.57 DZ 128 s 118 s 0.92 72 s 62 s 0.86 cc-pVDZ 398 s 274 s 0.69 308 s 185 s 0.60 Hessian 评估：P II${}^{xy}$ P 项 旧版 新版 新版/旧版 旧版 新版 新版/旧版 3-21G 294 s 136 s 0.46 238 s 100 s 0.42 6-31G** 2520 s 976 s 0.39 2065 s 828 s 0.40 DZ 631 s 332 s 0.53 600 s 230 s 0.38 cc-pVDZ 3202 s 1192 s 0.37 2715 s 866 s 0.32

表 A.1：AIX 计时数据来自运行 AIX4 操作系统的 IBM RS/6000 工作站，Linux 计时数据来自 Opteron 集群。

docs.title: A.3.1 概述
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

AOInts 经过优化构建，能够针对给定的积分类别和批次（batch）选择用于电子排斥积分（Electron Repulsion Integral, ERI）计算的最快积分算法。因此，程序未向用户提供用于覆盖其选择过程的必要变量。不过，用户可以在壳层对形成过程（METECO）中控制截断精度（cutoff）以及积分阈值（THRESH）。此外，用户还可以强制使用直接自洽场（Direct SCF）算法（DIRECT_SCF），并增大积分存储缓冲区的默认大小（INCORE_INTS_BUFFER）。

目前，Q-Chem 的某些线性标度（linear scaling）算法，例如 QCTC 和 ONX 算法，需要用户显式指定才能使用。预计随着研究的进一步发展，将能够识别出适合自动选择这些算法（或这些算法与其他算法的组合）的应用场景，正如 PRISM 算法会为给定积分类别选择最高效的计算路径一样，届时 Q-Chem 也能以类似方式自动完成算法选择。

docs.title: B.1.1 引言
docs.text:
(July 4, 2026)

  • 用户可以按任意顺序输入各个输入段（input section）；完整的输入段列表参见表 3.1。
  • 每个输入段都必须以 $end 结束。
  • 并非所有输入段都是必需的，但 \(rem* 和 *\)molecule 是必须提供的。
  • 整个 Q-Chem 输入均不区分大小写。
  • 多个作业（job）之间通过单独一行上的字符串 @@@ 分隔。

docs.title: B.1.2 Q-Chem 部分输入段的说明
B.1.2 Q-Chem 部分输入段的说明
B.1.2.1 $molecule
docs.text:
共有四种方法可用于输入几何结构信息：

  • Z-矩阵（单位为埃 Ångstrom 和度）：

$molecule

[电荷] [自旋多重度]

[Z-矩阵]

[若使用变量，则需空行]

[Z-矩阵变量（若使用）]

$end - 笛卡尔坐标（Cartesian Coordinates，单位为埃 Ångstrom）：

$molecule

[电荷] [自旋多重度]

[笛卡尔坐标]

[若使用变量，则需空行]

[坐标变量（若使用）]

$end - 从先前的计算中读取：

$molecule

read

$end - 从文件中读取：

$molecule

read filename

$end

docs.title: B.1.2.2 $rem
docs.text:
另请参见本附录末尾的 $rem 变量列表。其一般格式为：

$rem
   REM_VARIABLE   VALUE   [optional comment]
$end

不过，采用 "REM_VARIABLE = VALUE" 的写法也是可以接受的，即等号会被忽略。

docs.title: B.1.2.3 $basis
docs.text:
用户自定义基组（Basis Set）输入段的格式如下：

$basis \(X\) 0 \(L\) \(K\) \(scale\) \(\alpha_{1}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{1}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\alpha_{2}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{2}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\vdots\) \(\ddots\) \(\vdots\) \(\alpha_{K}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}}\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{min}}+1}\) \(\ldots\) \(C_{K}^{L_{\text{max}}}\) **** $end

其中

\(X\) 原子的元素符号（不接受原子序数）

\(L\) 角动量符号（S、P、SP、D、F、G）

\(K\) 壳层（shell）的收缩度（整数）

\(scale\) 应用于指数的缩放因子（默认值为 1.00）

\(a_{i}\) 高斯原函数（primitive）指数（正实数）

$C_{i}^{L} 每个角动量对应的收缩系数（非零实数）。

每个原子以 **** 结束，完整基组以 $end 关键字结束。基组一般输入中不能包含任何空行。注意，对于 SP 之类的复合壳层，每行需要包含不止一个收缩系数。与所有 Q-Chem 输入文件中的信息一样，所有输入均不区分大小写。

docs.title: B.1.2.4 $comment
docs.text:
用户可以在关键字输入段之外向输入文件添加注释，程序会将其忽略。这可以作为给用户自己的提醒，或者当需要教另一位用户编写输入文件时很有用。注释也可以放在 $comment 块中提供，不过鉴于整个输入文件都会被复制到输出文件中，这一做法实际上是多余的。

$comment
   User comments - copied to output file
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.5 $ecp
docs.text:
`$ecp

`对于每个带有赝势（ECP）的原子：

原子的化学符号

赝势（ECP）名称；该赝势的 \(L\) 值；被移除的核心电子数

对于每个赝势分量（按以下顺序：非投影分量、\(\hat{P}_{0}\)、\(\hat{P}_{1}\)、…、\(\hat{P}_{L-1}\)）

分量名称

该分量中高斯函数的数目

对于该分量中的每个高斯函数

\(r\) 的幂次；指数；收缩系数

****

$end

注意

(1) $ecp 块中的所有信息均不区分大小写。 (2) \(L\) 值不得超过 4。也就是说，不允许使用超出 \(G\) 的投影算符。 (3) \(r\) 的幂次（包含雅可比行列式 \(r^{2}\) 因子）必须为 0、1 或 2。

docs.title: B.1.2.6 $empirical_dispersion
docs.text:
$empirical_dispersion
    S6 S6_value
    D D_value
    C6 element_1 C6_value_for_element_1 element_2 C6_value_for_element_2
    VDW_RADII element_1 radii_for_element_1 element_2 radii_for_element_2
$end

注意

本段仅用于用户希望修改 Grimme 推荐的默认值的场合。

docs.title: B.1.2.7 $external_charges
docs.text:
如果输入文件中存在 \(external_charges* 关键字，Q-Chem 会扫描一组待纳入计算的外部点电荷。其格式如下所示，由笛卡尔坐标和点电荷的数值组成，每个电荷占一行。电荷单位为原子单位，坐标单位为埃（Ångstrom），除非通过将 *\)rem 关键字 INPUT_BOHR 设为 TRUE 而选择玻尔（bohr）为单位。外部电荷会随分子一起旋转到标准核取向，并按以下格式给出：

$external_charges
   x-coord1  y-coord1  z-coord1  charge1
   x-coord2  y-coord2  z-coord2  charge2
   x-coord3  y-coord3  z-coord3  charge3
$end

此外，用户可以使用关键字 ADD_CHARGED_CAGE 请求在分子周围添加一个带电笼（用于所谓的“电荷稳定化”计算）。详细信息请参见第 7.9.13 节。

docs.title: B.1.2.8 $intracule
docs.text:
$intracule

int_type 0 仅计算 \(P(u)\)

1 仅计算 \(M(v)\)

2 仅计算 \(W(u,v)\)

3 计算 \(P(u)\)、\(M(v)\) 和 \(W(u,v)\)

4 计算 \(P(u)\) 和 \(M(v)\)

5 计算 \(P(u)\) 和 \(W(u,v)\)

6 计算 \(M(v)\) 和 \(W(u,v)\)

u_points

点数、起点、终点。

v_points

点数、起点、终点。

moments 0–4 要计算的矩（moment）的阶数（仅用于 \(P(u)\)）。

derivs 0–4 要计算的导数的阶数（仅用于 \(P(u)\)）。

accuracy \(n\) （\(10^{-n})\) 指定内积数（intracule）插值表的精度（仅用于 \(P(u)\)）。

$end

docs.title: B.1.2.9 $isotopes
docs.text:
注意，质量应以原子单位（atomic units）给出。

$isotopes
   number_extra_loops  tp_flag
      number_of_atoms  [temp pressure]
      atom_number1 mass1
      atom_number2 mass2
   ...
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.10 $multipole_field
docs.text:
可以通过指定 $multipole_field 输入段，对所研究的分子施加多极场（multipole field）。该段中的每一行包含所施加场的一个单一分量，格式如下：

$multipole_field
   field_component_1   value_1
   field_component_2   value_2
$end

每个 field_component 采用笛卡尔（Cartesian）表示法指定：偶极场分量用 \(x\)、\(y\) 或 \(z\) 表示；四极场分量用 \(xx\)、\(xy\) 等表示，依此类推（\(\ldots\)）。每个场分量的数值应以原子单位提供。与许多教科书中的约定相反，在 Q-Chem 中，电场线被定义为从负电荷指向正电荷。[1235]

偶极场分量也可以通过两个原子的编号后跟场的大小来指定。该场分量将始终与连接 atom1 和 atom2 的矢量平行，并随原子运动而跟随坐标变化。

$multipole_field
   atom1 atom2 value
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.11 $nbo
docs.text:
更多信息请参阅第 10 章以及 NBO 手册。注意，必须将 NBO $rem 变量设置为 ON 才能启动 NBO 程序包。

$nbo
   [ NBO options ]
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.13 $opt
docs.text:
注意，单位为埃（Ångstrom）和度。另请参阅本附录下一节中的汇总说明。

$opt
CONSTRAINT
stre  atom1  atom2  value
...
bend  atom1  atom2  atom3  value
...
outp  atom1  atom2  atom3  atom4  value
...
tors  atom1  atom2  atom3  atom4  value
...
linc  atom1  atom2  atom3  atom4  value
...
linp  atom1  atom2  atom3  atom4  value
...
ENDCONSTRAINT

FIXED
atom   coordinate_reference
...
ENDFIXED

DUMMY
idum   type   list_length   defining_list
...
ENDDUMMY

CONNECT
atom   list_length   list
...
ENDCONNECT
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.14 $svp
docs.text:
$svp
<KEYWORD>=<VALUE>, <KEYWORD>=<VALUE>,...
<KEYWORD>=<VALUE>
$end

例如，该输入段可以如下所示：

$svp
    RHOISO=0.001, DIELST=78.39, NPTLEB=110
$end

docs.title: B.1.2.16 $plots
docs.text:
$plots

一行注释

在三行中指定三维点网格：

\(N_{x}\quad x_{\mathrm{min}}\quad x_{\mathrm{max}}\)

\(N_{y}\quad y_{\mathrm{min}}\quad y_{\mathrm{max}}\)

\(N_{z}\quad z_{\mathrm{min}}\quad z_{\mathrm{max}}\)

一行包含 4 个整数，指示要绘制的对象数量：

\(N_{\mathrm{MO}}\quad N_{\mathrm{Rho}}\quad N_{\mathrm{Trans}}\quad N_{\mathrm{DA}}\)

一行可选的整数列表，给出要计算的分子轨道（MO）编号（仅当 \(N_{\mathrm{MO}}>0\) 时）

MO(1)  MO(2) \(\ldots\) MO(\(N_{\mathrm{MO}}\))

一行可选的整数列表，给出要计算的密度（仅当 \(N_{\mathrm{Rho}}>0\) 时）

Rho(1)  Rho(2) \(\ldots\) Rho(\(N_{\mathrm{Rho}}\))

一行可选的整数列表，给出要计算的跃迁密度（仅当 \(N_{\mathrm{Trans}}>0\) 时）

Trans(1)  Trans(2) \(\ldots\) Trans(\(N_{\mathrm{Trans}}\))

一行可选的状态列表，用于电离/附着密度（detachment/attachment densities）（若 \(N_{\mathrm{DA}}>0\)）

DA(1)  DA(2) \(\ldots\) DA(\(N_{\mathrm{DA}}\))

$end

docs.title: B.1.2.17 $localized_diabatization
docs.text:
$localized_diabatization

   一行注释。

   一行列出需要混合的绝热态（adiabatic states）数组。

\(<adiabat1>\;\;\;\;\;\;\;<adiabat2>\;\;\;\;\;\;\;<adiabat3>\) \(\ldots\)

$end

**注意： 

绝热态的计数方式为：第一激发态对应 \(<adiabat>=1\)，第五激发态对应 \(<adiabat>=5\)，依此类推。 **

docs.text:
**注意： 

所有半径均以埃（Ångstroms）为单位给出。 **

$van_der_waals
   1
   atomic_number   VdW_radius
$end

$end

docs.title: B.2.2 含一般约束的几何优化
B.2.2 含一般约束的几何优化
docs.text:
（2026 年 7 月 4 日）

CONSTRAINT 和 ENDCONSTRAINT 分别界定 $opt 中约束区段的起始与结束，用户可在该区段内指定多达六种不同类型的约束：

原子间距离（interatomic distances）

取值单位为埃（Ångstroms）；value \(>0\)：

`stre atom1 atom2 value

`

键角（angles）

取值单位为度，\(0\leq value\leq 180\)；atom2 为该弯曲角的中心原子：

`bend atom1 atom2 atom3 value

`

面外弯曲角（out–of–plane–bends）

取值单位为度，\(-180\leq value\leq 180\) atom2；指 atom4 与 atom1–atom2–atom3 平面之间的夹角：

`outp atom1 atom2 atom3 atom4 value

`

二面角（dihedral angles）

取值单位为度，\(-180\leq value\leq 180\)；指 atom1–atom2–atom3 平面与 atom2–atom3–atom4 平面之间的夹角：

`tors atom1 atom2 atom3 atom4 value

`

共面弯曲角（coplanar bends）

取值单位为度，\(-180\leq value\leq 180\)；指 atom1–atom2–atom3 在 atom2–atom3–atom4 平面内的弯曲：

`linc atom1 atom2 atom3 atom4 value

`

垂直弯曲角（perpendicular bends）

取值单位为度，\(-180\leq value\leq 180\)；指 atom1–atom2–atom3 相对于 atom2–atom3–atom4 平面的垂直弯曲：

`linp atom1 atom2 atom3 atom4 value

`

绝对原子位置可以通过 FIXED 区段进行固定。该区段首行为 FIXED 关键字，末行为 ENDFIXED 关键字。固定某个原子的坐标的格式为：

atom coordinate_reference

coordinate_reference 可以是最多三个字符 \(X\)、\(Y\) 和 \(Z\) 的任意组合，用于指定要固定的坐标：\(X\)、\(Y\)、\(Z\)、XY、XZ、YZ、XYZ。固定字符必须相邻。例如：

FIXED
2 XY
ENDFIXED

  • 建议：使用默认值，最大误差提供了更可靠的判据。

docs.title: DIIS_SUBSPACE_SIZE
docs.text:
控制 SCF 过程中 DIIS 子空间的大小。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：10
  • 选项：
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议：无。

docs.title: DIRECT_DIAG
docs.text:
执行直接对角化以求得所有的 NEO 激发能。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • 执行直接对角化。
    • 0
    • 使用 Davidson 算法。
  • 建议：仅在 Davidson 解不稳定时使用此选项。

docs.title: DISTORT
docs.text:
指定是否对化学体系施加压力或外力

  • 类型：LOGICAL
  • 默认值：False
  • 选项：
    • False
    • 不使用压力或力
    • True
    • 使用压力或力
  • 建议：设置为 true 以施加压力或力。

docs.title: EDA2_MOM
docs.text:
使用 MOM 对非构造原理（non-aufbau）电子组态执行 ALMO-EDA 计算

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • FALSE
    • 标准 ALMO-EDA 计算
    • TRUE
    • 针对非
    • 构造原理
    • 态的 ALMO-EDA
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EDA_ALIGN_FRGM_SPIN
docs.text:
开启片段自旋对齐程序

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 0
    • 不执行自旋对齐程序（在非限制情形下默认开启）
    • 1
    • 执行片段自旋对齐；在 MOM 计算之前的极化步骤中使用 GDM
    • 2
    • 执行片段自旋对齐；在极化步骤中使用 GDM 并进行稳定性分析
  • 建议：当自由基具有高度对称结构时使用 1 或 2

docs.title: EDA_NOCV
docs.text:
执行 NOCV 分析并绘制显著的 NOCV

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 0
    • 不执行 NOCV 分析
    • 1
    • 绘制 NOCV 对密度形变的成对贡献
    • 2
    • 同时绘制 NOCV 对密度形变的成对贡献和 NOCV 轨道
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EDA_PLOT_DIFF_DEN
docs.text:
绘制由于极化（POL）和电荷转移（CT）引起的电子密度变化

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • FALSE
    • 不绘制 EDD 图
    • TRUE
    • 绘制 EDD 图
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EIGSLV_METH
docs.text:
控制求解 ALMO-CIS 本征方程的方法

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 0
    • 显式构建哈密顿量然后对角化（全谱）
    • 1
    • 使用 Davidson 方法（目前仅对限制情形可用）
  • 建议：无；在 ALMO-TDA 计算中使用 1（0 不可用）

docs.title: EMB_DIPOLE
docs.text:
触发迭代偶极矩的计算

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • FALSE
    • 不计算迭代偶极矩
    • TRUE
    • 计算迭代偶极矩
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EMB_ITER
docs.text:
开启基于投影的迭代密度嵌入

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • FALSE
    • 不对不同片段进行迭代。
    • TRUE
    • 开启迭代密度嵌入。
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EMB_POL
docs.text:
触发迭代极化率张量的计算

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • FALSE
    • 不计算迭代极化率张量
    • TRUE
    • 计算迭代极化率张量
  • 建议：无

docs.title: ENV_METHOD
docs.text:
指定基于投影的嵌入计算中的低级别理论方法

  • 类型：STRING
  • 默认值：NONE
  • 选项：
    • 解析方式与
    • $rem
    • 变量 “
    • METHOD
    • ”
    • 相同
  • 建议：应选择平均场方法（纯密度泛函或杂化密度泛函）。

docs.title: EOM_DIIS_CONVERGENCE
docs.text:
求解实值 EOM 态的 DIIS 算法收敛判据（仅适用于 LIBGMBPT 中的 RI-CC2）。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：5
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • 对应于
    • \(10^{-n}\)
    • 收敛判据。
  • 建议：过松的收敛判据可能导致找到错误的态。

docs.title: EOM_DIIS_MAXVECTORS
docs.text:
指定 DIIS 子空间的最大规模（仅适用于 LIBGMBPT 中的 RI-CC2）。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：7
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • DIIS 子空间中最多
    • \(n\)
    • 个向量。
  • 建议：较大的值会增加磁盘存储，但能加快并稳定收敛。

docs.title: EOM_DIIS_MAX_ITER
docs.text:
DIIS 过程允许的最大迭代次数（仅适用于 LIBGMBPT 中的 RI-CC2）。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：100
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • 用户自定义的迭代次数。
  • 建议：默认值通常已足够。

docs.title: EP_FACTOR
docs.text:
控制 NEO-MP2 相关能中电子-质子分量的强度。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：1000000
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • 对应于
    • \(c_{\mathrm{ep}}=n/10^{6}\)
    • 。
  • 建议：无

docs.title: ESP_EFIELD
docs.text:
触发在核位置或给定网格点上计算静电势（ESP）和/或电场

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 0
    • 仅计算 ESP
    • 1
    • 同时计算 ESP 和电场
    • 2
    • 仅计算电场
  • 建议：无

docs.title: EX_EDA
docs.text:
对一个或多个片段处于激发态的体系执行 ALMO-EDA 计算。

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE
    • 执行考虑激发态分子的 EDA 计算。
    • FALSE
  • 建议：无

docs.title: FIXING_V_EMBED
docs.text:
对嵌入计算所用的能量泛函调用线性化近似

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：TRUE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE
    • 对能量泛函使用线性化近似 [公式 (
    • 11.106
    • )]
    • FALSE
    • 使用原始能量泛函 [公式 (
    • 11.100
    • )]
  • 建议：使用默认值以节省计算成本

docs.title: FODFT_DONOR
docs.text:
指定 FODFT 计算中的给体（donor）片段

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：1
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • 第一个片段作为给体
    • 2
    • 第二个片段作为给体
  • 建议：当 FODFT_METHOD = 1 时，带电片段需作为给体片段

docs.title: FODFT_METHOD
docs.text:
指定 FODFT 方法的具体形式

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：1
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • FODFT(
    • \(\mathrm{2n-1}\)
    • )@
    • \(D^{+}A\)
    • (HT) / FODFT(
    • \(\mathrm{2n+1}\)
    • )@
    • \(D^{-}A\)
    • (ET)
    • 2
    • FODFT(
    • \(\mathrm{2n}\)
    • )@
    • \(DA\)
    • 3
    • FODFT(
    • \(\mathrm{2n-1}\)
    • )@
    • \(DA\)
    • (HT) / FODFT(
    • \(\mathrm{2n+1}\)
    • )@
    • \(D^{-}A^{-}\)
    • (ET)
  • 建议：默认方法显示出最佳的整体性能

docs.title: FRAG_DIABAT_DOHT
docs.text:
指定考虑的是空穴转移还是电子转移

  • 类型：BOOLEAN
  • 默认值：TRUE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE
    • 执行空穴转移
    • FALSE
    • 执行电子转移
  • 建议：在 POD 和 FODFT 计算中需要指定

docs.title: FRAG_DIABAT_METHOD
docs.text:
指定基于片段的绝热化（diabatization）方法

  • 类型：STRING
  • 默认值：NONE
  • 选项：
    • ALMO_MSDFT
    • 执行 ALMO(MSDFT) 绝热化
    • POD
    • 执行投影算符绝热化（原始方法）
    • POD2_L
    • 执行采用 Löwdin 正交化的 POD2
    • POD2_GS
    • 执行采用 Gram-Schmidt 正交化的 POD2
    • ESID
    • 二聚体能量分裂法（energy-split-in-dimer method），
    • 1384
    • Valeev E. F. 等，
    • J. Am. Chem. Soc.
    • (2006)
    • ，
    • 128
    • ，
    • 第 9882 页
    • 。
    • 链接
    • 该方法等价于第
    • 节中介绍的
    • FMO 方法
  • 建议：无

docs.title: FRAG_DIABAT_PRINT
docs.text:
指定基于碎片的绝热化（diabatization）计算的打印级别

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 0
  • 可选值:
    • 0: 不输出额外信息 \(\geq 1\) 输出额外详细信息
  • 建议: 除非需要调试信息，否则使用默认值

docs.title: GAP_TOL
docs.text:
HOMO/LUMO 能隙阈值，用于控制是否对 Fock 矩阵虚轨道块的对角元素进行平移（level shift）。如果在某次 SCF 迭代中 HOMO/LUMO 能隙小于该阈值，则对 Fock 矩阵虚轨道块的对角元素施加平移；否则不施加能级平移（level-shift）。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 300
  • 可选值:
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议: 输入数值必须是 0 到 9999 之间的整数。实际施加的阈值等于输入值除以 1000（单位为 Eh）。默认值仅用于保证能级平移计算能够运行，不应视为任何具体问题的最优值，可能需要反复尝试才能找到最佳阈值。该值越大，通常意味着在 SCF 收敛过程中越频繁地使用能级平移。

docs.title: GEN_SCFMAN_EMBED
docs.text:
使用基于 GEN_SCFMAN 的实现来运行基于投影的嵌入（embedding）计算

  • 类型: BOOLEAN
  • 默认值: FALSE
  • 可选值:
    • TRUE: 执行基于投影的嵌入计算
    • FALSE: 不执行嵌入计算
  • 建议: 无

docs.title: GUESS_GRID
docs.text:
指定生成 SAP 初始猜测时所使用的网格类型。可选项与 $rem 变量 XC_GRID 相同。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 1
  • 可选值:
    • 0: 对 H、C、N、O 使用 SG-0 网格，对其余所有原子使用 SG-1 网格。
    • \(n\): 对所有原子使用 SG-
    • \(n\): 网格， \(n=1,2\) 或 3 \(XY\) 由两个六位整数组成的字符串 \(X\) 和 \(Y\)，其中 \(X\) 为径向点数， \(Y\) 为角向点数（角向点数须为第 5.5 节表 5.2 中允许的 Lebedev 角向点数值）。 \(-XY\) Gauss-Legendre 网格采用类似格式，六位整数 \(X\) 对应径向点数，六位整数 \(Y\) 给出 Gauss-Legendre 角向点数， \(Y=2N^{2}\)。
  • 建议: 如果 SAP 初始猜测质量较差，可能需要使用更大的网格。

docs.title: JOBTYPE
docs.text:
指定计算类型。

  • 类型: STRING
  • 默认值: SP
  • 可选值:
    • SP: 单点能计算。 FORCE 解析梯度（受力）计算。
    • OPT: 几何结构优化（极小化）。
    • TS: 过渡态搜索。 FREQ 频率计算。
  • 建议: 视具体应用而定。进行几何结构优化时请始终设置 POINT_GROUP_SYMMETRY = FALSE。

docs.title: LEVEL_SHIFT
docs.text:
决定在与 DIIS 联用时是否启用能级平移（level-shifting）。

  • 类型: LOGICAL
  • 默认值: FALSE
  • 可选值:
    • TRUE: 施加能级平移。
    • FALSE: 不施加能级平移。
  • 建议: 如果需要借助能级平移来加速 SCF 收敛，则设置为 TRUE。

docs.title: LSHIFT
docs.text:
对 Fock 矩阵虚轨道块所有对角元素施加的恒定平移量。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 200
  • 可选值:
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议: 输入数值必须是 0 到 9999 之间的整数。实际平移量等于输入值除以 1000（单位为 Eh）。默认值仅用于保证能级平移计算能够运行，不应视为任何具体问题的最优值，可能需要反复尝试才能找到最佳阈值。较大的平移量使 SCF 过程更稳定，但也会减慢收敛速度，从而需要更多的 SCF 迭代循环。

docs.title: MAX_DP_CYCLES
docs.text:
当 SCF_ALGORITHM = DP_DIIS 和 DP_GDM 时，使用阻尼（damping）的 SCF 迭代最大次数。另见 THRESH_DP_SWITCH 。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 3
  • 可选值:
    • 1: 仅单步 SCF 使用阻尼，其余 SCF 步骤不使用阻尼。
    • \(n\): 在关闭阻尼之前，进行 \(n\) 次带阻尼的 SCF 迭代。
  • 建议: 如果关闭阻尼后仍存在剧烈震荡，可增大此数值。

docs.title: MAX_LS_CYCLES
docs.text:
当 SCF_ALGORITHM = LS_DIIS 时，使用能级平移的 DIIS 迭代最大次数。另见 THRESH_LS_SWITCH 。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: MAX_SCF_CYCLES
  • 可选值:
    • 1: 仅单步 DIIS 使用能级平移，其余 DIIS 步骤不使用能级平移。
    • \(n\): 在关闭能级平移之前，进行 \(n\) 次带能级平移的 DIIS 迭代。
  • 建议: 无

docs.title: MAX_SCF_CYCLES
docs.text:
控制允许的最大 SCF 迭代次数。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 50
  • 可选值:
    • \(n\): \(n>0\) 用户自行选择。
  • 建议: 对于收敛缓慢的体系（例如含过渡金属的体系），应增大该值。

docs.title: MEM_STATIC
docs.text:
为 Q-Chem 4.1 及更早版本中的 AO 积分求值及其变换设置内存。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 192
  • 可选值:
    • \(n\): 用户自定义的内存大小（兆字节，MB）。
  • 建议: 使用默认值。

docs.title: MEM_TOTAL
docs.text:
设置 Q-Chem 可用的总内存（单位：兆字节，MB）。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 2000
  • 可选值:
    • \(n\): 用户自定义的内存大小（兆字节，MB）。
  • 建议: 使用默认值，或设置为机器的物理内存大小。最低要求为 \(3X^{2}\) 。

docs.title: METHOD
docs.text:
指定交换-关联泛函。

  • 类型: STRING
  • 默认值: 无默认值
  • 可选值:
    • NAME: 使用 = NAME，其中 NAME 为以下之一： HF 表示 Hartree-Fock 理论； 第 5.3.5 节所列的某种 DFT 方法；
  • 建议: 一般而言，请参考相关文献指导选择。我们对 DFT 方法的推荐在第 5.3.5 节中以粗体标出。

docs.title: MOM_METHOD
docs.text:
确定在每次 SCF 迭代中与之最大化重叠的目标轨道。

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: MOM
  • 可选值:
    • MOM: 与上一轮 SCF 迭代的轨道最大化重叠。
    • IMOM: 与初始猜测轨道最大化重叠。
  • 建议: 若能获得合适的猜测轨道，则 IMOM 可以更可靠地收敛到目标解。75 Barca G. M. J., Gilbert A. T. B., Gill P. M. W. J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2018) , 14 , pp. 1501 . 链接

docs.title: MSDFT_METHOD
docs.text:
指定 ALMO(MSDFT) 所使用的方案

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 2
  • 可选值:
    • 1: 原始 MSDFT 方案 [式 ( 10.208 )]
    • 2: ALMO(MSDFT2) 方法 [式 ( 10.211 )]
  • 建议: 使用默认方法。注意，如果请求使用 meta-GGA 泛函，该方法将被自动重置为 1。

docs.title: MSDFT_PINV_THRESH
docs.text:
设置态间（interstate）重叠矩阵伪逆的阈值

  • 类型: INTEGER
  • 默认值: 4
  • 可选值:
    • \(n\): 将阈值设置为 10 \({}^{-n}\)
  • 建议: 使用默认值

docs.title: NADD_XMETHOD
docs.text:
允许基于用户自定义的 XC 泛函来构建嵌入势，独立于获得超体系密度时所使用的交换-关联泛函。

  • 类型: STRING
  • 默认值: None
  • 可选值:
    • None: 使用与描述环境相同的交换-关联泛函来构建嵌入势。
    • GEN: 需要提供 $nadd_xc_functional 区段来指定所使用的非加和（non-additive）交换-关联泛函。 $nadd_xc_functional 区段的构造方式如下所示。该区段的每一行需要三个变量：X 或 C，用于指明该分量属于交换（exchange）还是关联（correlation）；泛函的符号表示（与 EXCHANGE 或 CORRELATION 关键字变量所取的写法相同），以及每个分量的实数系数（格式详情参见第 5.3.7 节）。
  • 建议: 无

docs.title: NDAMP
docs.text:
确定混合系数 \(\alpha\) = /100。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：75
  • 选项：
    • 用户自定义。0 到 100 之间的整数。
  • 建议：如果在自洽场（SCF）过程中出现强烈波动，则增大该值。

docs.title: NEO_BASIS_LIN_DEP_THRESH
docs.text:
该关键字用于设置核基组的线性相关阈值。其定义为 \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_BASIS\_LIN\_DEP\_THRESH}}\) 。

  • 类型：DOUBLE
  • 默认值：5.0
  • 选项：
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议：无建议。

docs.title: NEO_BOMD
docs.text:
执行一次 NEO-BOMD 模拟。

  • 类型：LOGICAL/INTEGER
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE（或 1）
    • 启用 NEO-BOMD。
    • FALSE（或 0）
    • 禁用 NEO-BOMD。
  • 建议：每一步中质子基函数中心的优化由第 9.2.2 节讨论的常规 $rem 变量控制。通常需要将 GEOM_OPT_TOL_GRADIENT \(=30\) 设为该值，以便在长时间尺度上保持足够的能量守恒。325 Dickinson J. A. et al. J. Chem. Phys. (2026) , 164 , pp. 234108 . 链接

docs.title: NEO_CC2
docs.text:
启用 NEO-CC2 计算。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • 启用此选项。
    • 0
    • 禁用此选项。
  • 建议：默认执行基态 NEO-CC2 计算。可通过 SET_ROOTS 变量启用激发态。

docs.title: NEO_CCSD_CONVERGENCE
docs.text:
当能量误差小于 \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_CCSD\_CONVERGENCE}}\) 时，认为 NEO-RICCSD 已收敛。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：8
  • 选项：
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议：无

docs.title: NEO_CCSD_MAX_CYCLES
docs.text:
控制允许的最大 CC 迭代次数。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：5000
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • 将最大迭代次数设置为
    • \(n>0\)
    • 。
  • 建议：无

docs.title: NEO_ELMD
docs.text:
执行一次 NEO-ELMD 模拟。

  • 类型：LOGICAL/INTEGER
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE（或 1）
    • 启用 NEO-ELMD。
    • FALSE（或 0）
    • 禁用 NEO-ELMD。
  • 建议：若要在长时间尺度上进行模拟，请运行 NEO-ELMD 而非 NEO-BOMD。

docs.title: NEO_EPC
docs.text:
指定电子-质子关联泛函。

  • 类型：STRING
  • 默认值：无默认值
  • 选项：
    • NAME
    • 使用
    • =
    • NAME
    • ，其中
    • NAME
    • 可以是 epc172 或 epc19。
  • 建议：请参考 NEO 相关文献以指导选择。

docs.title: NEO_E_CONV
docs.text:
NEO-SCF 计算中的能量收敛判据，即相邻两次迭代之间的能量差小于 \(10^{-\mathrm{NEO\_E\_CONV}}\) 。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：8
  • 选项：
    • 用户自定义
  • 建议：建议为几何优化采用更严格的收敛判据。注意，对于分步（stepwise）计算，该收敛判据检查的是电子微迭代块与质子微迭代块之间的能量差。

docs.title: NEO_E_MAX_SCF_CYCLES
docs.text:
控制允许的最大电子 SCF 微迭代次数。该变量仅用于分步 NEO-SCF 优化。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：150
  • 选项：
    • \(n\)
    • \(n>0\)
    • 用户选定。
  • 建议：无。

docs.title: NEO_ISOTOPE
docs.text:
启用不同类型同位素的计算。目前仅允许一种同位素类型。

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：1
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • 此 NEO 计算使用质子（protons）。
    • 2
    • 此 NEO 计算使用氘核（deuterons）。
    • 3
    • 此 NEO 计算使用氚核（tritons）。
  • 建议：有关同位素效应计算的最佳性能表现，请参考 NEO 相关文献。

docs.title: NEO_MSDFT
docs.text:
启用 NEO-MSDFT 计算

  • 类型：INTEGER
  • 默认值：0
  • 选项：
    • 1
    • 启用 NEO-MSDFT 计算。
    • 0
    • 禁用 NEO-MSDFT 计算。
  • 建议：有关自定义 NEO-MSDFT 计算的详细信息，请参见第 13.5.2.3 节。

docs.title: NEO_N_HARTREE_PROD
docs.text:
启用核哈特里积（Hartree product）近似。

  • 类型：LOGICAL/INTEGER
  • 默认值：FALSE
  • 选项：
    • TRUE（或 1）
    • 启用核哈特里积计算。
    • FALSE（或 0）
    • 禁用核哈特里积计算。
